definition_zh: 生命；生活；一生；寿命；活力
definition_en: the state of being alive; the way someone lives; the period from birth to death; energy and liveliness
core_image: 一株从破土、开花到枯萎的完整植物，一段有始有终的时间
scene: 产房外，祖父抱着刚出生的婴儿老泪纵横。 Some people find new life in a strange city.
sceneCN: 这里 life 是「生活方式」（第 2 个义项：生活）；句意为有些人在陌生城市里找到新的生活。

derivatives.zh: life 与 time 合成，指「一生；终身期间」
life 与 long 合成，指「终身的；毕生的」
life 加 -less，指「无生命的；死气沉沉的」

senses.title: The state of being alive
senses.definition: the quality that distinguishes living things from dead matter
senses.definitionCN: 把生物与死物区分开来的性质
senses.example: Doctors fought all night to save the patient\u0027s life.
senses.exampleCN: 医生整夜奋战抢救病人性命。
senses.why: Breath, growth and repair mark the living from the stone; the word names that difference.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸、生长与修复区分生命与石头，这个词就命名这种差异。

senses.title: The way a person lives
senses.definition: the activities, work and pleasures of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体的活动、工作与乐趣
senses.example: Some people find new life in a strange city.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人在陌生城市里找到新的生活。
senses.why: Being alive happens in a certain way, so the state became the manner.
senses.whyCN: 活着总是以某种方式进行，状态于是变成了方式。

senses.title: The period from birth to death
senses.definition: the time between birth and death
senses.definitionCN: 从出生到死亡之间的时间
senses.example: She spent her life teaching in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 她一生都在山里教书。
senses.why: A life can be counted in years, so the state turned into a length of time.
senses.whyCN: 生命可以用年头计，状态于是变成时间长度。

senses.title: Liveliness and energy
senses.definition: energy, excitement or liveliness
senses.definitionCN: 精力、兴奋或生气
senses.example: The party suddenly came to life after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜后派对突然热闹起来。
senses.why: Full life shows as movement and brightness, so energy borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 充沛的生命表现为活动与光亮，活力便借用了这个名字。

senses.title: The duration of something useful
senses.definition: how long a machine, product or organization works
senses.definitionCN: 机器、产品或机构可用多久
senses.example: The battery has a life of five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这块电池的寿命是五年。
senses.why: Machines live and die like bodies, so the word spread to objects.
senses.whyCN: 机器像身体一样生灭，词便扩及器物。

senses.title: Living things collectively
senses.definition: living creatures and plants considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的动植物
senses.example: Ocean life is still largely unknown.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物仍大多不为人知。
senses.why: All living things together form one subject, the science of life.
senses.whyCN: 一切生物合在一起成为一个主题——生命科学。

senses.title: A biography
senses.definition: a written account of a person\u0027s life
senses.definitionCN: 记述某人一生的文字
senses.example: He wrote a life of the poet.
senses.exampleCN: 他写了一部诗人传记。
senses.why: A whole span of years fills a book, so the time became the story.
senses.whyCN: 一生岁月填满一本书，时间于是变成故事。

intro.en: Life comes from Old English lif, from Germanic roots of remaining and continuing; the same family gives live and the leave-behind words.
intro.cn: life 来自古英语 lif，出自日耳曼语「留存、延续」词根；live 与「留下」诸词同出此族。

items.en: Old English lif meant 'life', and the verb libban 'to live' grew beside it.
items.cn: 古英语 lif 意为「生命」，动词 libban「活着」在旁生长。

items.en: Germanic roots of remaining and continuing lie behind the family: to live is to last.
items.cn: 「留存、延续」的日耳曼词根是词族的基础：活着即是延续。

items.en: In Middle English the plural lives settled, and 'life' came to mean a biography.
items.cn: 中古英语里复数 lives 固定下来，life 开始指传记。

items.en: Modern English widened life to machines, oceans and batteries.
items.cn: 现代英语把 life 扩展到机器、海洋与电池。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the trail beyond Germanic, perhaps meaning 'to remain', is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：日耳曼语之前或与「留存」相关的轨迹仍有争议。

note.en: Group one flags look-alikes; group two lists living and lasting words.
note.cn: 第一组标出形近词；第二组列出存活与延续之词。

entries.definition: To raise; shares three letters, unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 举起；共享三字母，词根无关。

entries.definition: The verb of the same family; life is its noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同族动词；life 是其名词。

entries.definition: The whole span of a life.
Being, especially bare survival; more abstract than life.
entries.definitionCN: 存在，尤指勉强维持；比 life 更抽象。

entries.definition: A written life; matches the biography sense.
The way one earns a living.
Energy and liveliness; matches the energy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 精力与生气；对应活力义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real family and fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实词族与固定搭配。

normal.en: Old English lif meant life; libban meant to live.
normal.cn: 古英语 lif 意为生命；libban 意为活着。

normal.en: Family: lives, lifetime, lifelong, lifeless.
normal.cn: 词族：lives、lifetime、lifelong、lifeless。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: daily life, come to life, in real life.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：日常生活、苏醒、在现实中。

normal.en: Batteries and machines have a life too.
normal.cn: 电池与机器也有「寿命」。

normal.en: A written life of someone is also called a life.
normal.cn: 记述某人一生的书也叫 a life。

abstract.en: Picture a seed cracking open under the soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子在土里破壳。

abstract.en: Picture an empty hall filling with music and people.
abstract.cn: 想象空旷大厅被音乐与人填满。

abstract.en: Picture a clock slowly winding down beside a machine.
abstract.cn: 想象机器旁的发条慢慢走完。

examples.en: Country life suits him better than the city.
examples.cn: 乡村生活比城市更适合他。

examples.en: The old town comes to life at festival time.
examples.cn: 节日期间老城生机盎然。

examples.en: She has spent her life collecting folk songs.
examples.cn: 她一生都在采集民歌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来夫」——来这世上，活成一夫当关的一生 → 生命；生活

root: 古英语 lif「生命」，出自日耳曼语「留存、延续」词根；与 live、德语 bleiben 词族有亲缘；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses all grow from continuing: being alive, the way of it, the length of it, its brightness, the life of machines, all living things, and the written life.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项都从「延续」生长：活着本身、活的方式、活的长度、它的光亮、机器之寿、众生整体与书写的生平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a span of time that keeps breathing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段持续呼吸的时光。

branches.en: THE BARE STATE: the difference between stone and seed.
branches.cn: 裸状态：石头与种子的分界。

branches.en: THE MANNER: living takes a shape, daily or chosen.
branches.cn: 方式：生活有其形状——日常的或自选的。

branches.en: THE SPAN: years counted, then written into a book.
branches.cn: 全程：以年计，再写成书。

branches.en: BRIGHTNESS AND DURATION: party energy, battery years.
branches.cn: 光亮与时长：派对的生气、电池的年头。

branches.en: EVERYTHING ALIVE: the whole living world as one subject.
branches.cn: 众生：整个生命世界作为一个主题。

intro.en: Life is a native word with no prefixes; the family compounds with time, long and less.
intro.cn: life 是无前缀的本族词；词族与 time、long、less 复合。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族复合词。

items.example: F changes to ves in the plural.
items.exampleCN: 复数时 f 变 ves。

definition_zh: 坚持；坚决要求；坚称
definition_en: to demand something firmly or keep saying that something is true
core_image: 双手撑地不肯挪动的双脚
scene: 孩子攥着书包带不肯松手。 She insisted on paying the bill herself.
sceneCN: 这里 insist 是「坚决要求」（第 2 个义项：坚定地索要）；句意：她坚持自己付账。

derivatives.zh: insist 加名词后缀，义为「坚持；执意」
insist 加形容词后缀，义为「急切的；坚持的」
换前缀的同根词，义为「持续；坚持不放弃」

senses.title: To demand firmly
senses.definition: to ask for something strongly and refuse to give up
senses.definitionCN: 强烈要求且不肯让步
senses.example: He insisted on an apology.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚决要求道歉。
senses.why: Both feet are planted and will not move.
senses.whyCN: 双脚扎根，寸步不让。

senses.title: To keep standing on
senses.definition: to keep taking a stand without yielding
senses.definitionCN: 坚守立场而不退让
senses.example: She insisted on her innocence.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚称自己无辜。
senses.why: The feet stay planted on one spot.
senses.whyCN: 双脚立定原地。

senses.title: To declare against doubt
senses.definition: to state something firmly while others disagree
senses.definitionCN: 在他人存疑时坚定地陈述
senses.example: He insisted that the door was locked.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚称门是锁着的。
senses.why: The voice repeats while hands point at the spot.
senses.whyCN: 手指出原地，声音反复重申。

senses.title: If you insist: polite yielding
senses.definition: a polite phrase meaning I agree because you demand it
senses.definitionCN: 表示因对方坚持而同意的客套话
senses.example: If you insist, I will take the window seat.
senses.exampleCN: 你坚持的话，我就坐靠窗吧。
senses.why: The feet step aside because the other's feet will not.
senses.whyCN: 对方的脚不移，自己的脚只好让开。

intro.en: Insist comes from Latin insistere, to stand upon, from in- (upon) and stare (to stand). To insist is literally to keep standing on your demand.
intro.cn: insist 来自拉丁语 insistere「站立其上」，由 in-「其上」+ stare「站立」构成；insist 字面就是一直站在你的要求上。

items.en: Latin stare meant to stand; it gave stay, statue and steady.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立；同根词有 stay、statue、steady。

items.en: in- plus stare formed insistere: to stand upon, to dwell on.
items.cn: in- 加 stare 构成 insistere：立于其上、执着于。

items.en: Insistere could mean to pause on or to persist in pressing.
items.cn: insistere 可指停留，也可指持续施压。

items.en: Old French insister passed the sense of pressing a demand.
items.cn: 古法语 insister 传递「施压索求」之义。

items.en: Middle English insisten meant to pursue or dwell upon.
items.cn: 中古英语 insisten 意为追索、执着于。

items.en: Modern English settled the demand and declare senses.
items.cn: 现代英语定型了索求与坚称两义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the stand-root family. The meaning group compares words of holding firm.
note.cn: 形近组收录「站立」词根词族；词义组比较表示坚守的词。

entries.definition: the noun for firm demands.
to keep on through time.
to stand against.
to ask with force.
to keep asserting.
to refuse to yield.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing root, the insist-on pattern and the polite phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「站立」词根、insist on 句式与客套用语。

normal.en: in- plus stare (stand): keep standing on your point.
normal.cn: in- 加 stare（站立）：一直站在你的立场上。

normal.en: insist on plus noun is the exam pattern.
normal.cn: insist on 加名词是考试句式。

normal.en: persist is the patient twin; resist the fighting twin.
normal.cn: persist 是耐心的孪生词，resist 是对抗的孪生词。

normal.en: if you insist softens the firmness politely.
normal.cn: if you insist 客气地软化坚持。

normal.en: statue and stay share the standing root.
normal.cn: statue 与 stay 共享站立词根。

abstract.en: One image: shoes rooted to the floor while the room argues.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：满屋争论，鞋跟却长进地板。

abstract.en: To insist is to be a statue with a voice.
abstract.cn: insist 就是有声音的雕像。

abstract.en: The clock ticks; the feet stay.
abstract.cn: 钟在走，脚不动。

examples.en: He insisted that the report be rewritten.
examples.cn: 他坚持要求重写报告。

examples.en: I insisted on seeing the manager.
examples.cn: 我坚持要见经理。

examples.en: If you insist, we can leave tonight.
examples.cn: 你坚持的话，我们今晚就走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因西斯特」：西边的铁塔一直「立」着不倒， insist。

root: 拉丁语 in-「其上」+ stare「站立」→ insistere「立于其上、执着于」→ 古法语 insister → 中古英语 insisten → 现代英语 insist；同根词 persist、resist、stay、statue。

sensesIntro.en: Insist is planted feet: a demand that will not move, a stand held under doubt, a voice that repeats, and a polite step aside.
sensesIntro.cn: insist 是扎了根的脚：不让步的要求、存疑下的坚守、反复重申的声音，以及客气的让步。

core.en: Standing on your own point until the world moves or you do.
core.cn: 站在自己的立场上，直到世界让步或你让步。

branches.en: DEMAND: insisted on an apology.
branches.cn: 索求：坚决要求道歉。

branches.en: STAND: insisted on her innocence.
branches.cn: 立场：坚称无辜。

branches.en: ASSERTION: insisted that the door was locked.
branches.cn: 断言：坚称门锁着。

branches.en: YIELDING: if you insist, the window seat.
branches.cn: 让步：你坚持就坐窗边。

branches.en: PRESSURE: feet planted, voice repeated.
branches.cn: 施压：脚立定，声音反复。

intro.en: Insist builds insistence, insistent and its standing twins persist and resist.
intro.cn: insist 构成 insistence、insistent 及孪生词 persist、resist。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the standing verb stare behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的站立动词 stare。

definition_zh: 不久；快；一……就
definition_en: in a short time from now, early, or as soon as
core_image: 站台上的人抬头望着远处，火车灯已经出现在拐弯处
scene: 火车不久就要到了。 The train will arrive soon.
sceneCN: 这里 soon 是「不久」（第 1 个义项）；句意：火车不久就要到了。

derivatives.zh: 更早；宁愿
最早

senses.title: In a short time
senses.definition: in a short time from now
senses.definitionCN: 从现在起很短的时间内
senses.example: The train will arrive soon.
senses.exampleCN: 火车不久就要到了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is at once or immediately.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是「立刻、马上」。

senses.title: Early
senses.definition: earlier than expected or usual
senses.definitionCN: 比预期或通常更早
senses.example: Do not leave too soon.
senses.exampleCN: 别走得太早。
senses.why: A short time before a point is an early arrival.
senses.whyCN: 在某个时间点前的一小段时间，就是提前到达。

senses.title: As soon as
senses.definition: immediately when something happens
senses.definitionCN: 某事一发生就立刻
senses.example: Call me as soon as you arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 你一到就给我打电话。
senses.why: The phrase fixes the sense of no delay at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语固定了「毫不耽搁」的含义。

intro.en: Soon first meant at once, and later meant in a short time.
intro.cn: soon 最初意为立刻，后来表示在短时间内。

items.en: Sona meant at once or immediately.
items.cn: sona 意为立刻或马上。

items.en: The form became soon.
items.cn: 词形变为 soon。

items.en: It softened to mean in a short time.
items.cn: 它的含义软化为「在短时间内」。

items.en: It also came to mean early.
items.cn: 它也开始表示「早」。

items.en: As soon as became a fixed phrase for no delay.
items.cn: as soon as 成为表示毫不耽搁的固定短语。

note.en: Soon is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of near time.
note.cn: 把 soon 与形近词以及表示临近时间的副词作比较。

entries.definition: a male child
a piece of music with words
twelve o'clock in the day
in a short time
at speed
soon, in a little while

normalIntro.en: Soon puts a small distance between now and then.
normalIntro.cn: soon 在现在与那时之间留出一小段距离。

normal.en: The train will arrive soon.
normal.cn: 火车不久就要到了。

normal.en: Do not leave too soon.
normal.cn: 别走得太早。

normal.en: Call me as soon as you arrive.
normal.cn: 你一到就给我打电话。

normal.en: Soon after the rain, the sun came out.
normal.cn: 雨后不久，太阳出来了。

normal.en: Sooner or later, the truth appears.
normal.cn: 真相迟早会显现。

abstract.en: Soon is the word for a future already on its way.
abstract.cn: soon 是用来指「已经在路上的未来」的词。

abstract.en: Waiting makes soon feel long.
abstract.cn: 等待会让「不久」显得漫长。

abstract.en: What is done soon is often done twice.
abstract.cn: 太快做完的事，常常要再做一遍。

examples.en: The train will arrive soon.
examples.cn: 火车不久就要到了。

examples.en: Do not leave too soon.
examples.cn: 别走得太早。

examples.en: Soon after the rain, the sun came out.
examples.cn: 雨后不久，太阳出来了。

dict_mnemonic.text: soon 注意与 son（儿子）、song（歌）区分拼写；as soon as 是「一……就」，soon after 是「不久之后」，sooner or later 是「迟早」。

root: 来自古英语 sona（立刻），核心义从「马上」软化为「不久、很快」。

sensesIntro.en: Soon means in a short time, early, or immediately when something happens.
sensesIntro.cn: soon 意为不久、提早，或某事一发生就立刻。

core.en: A short distance ahead in time.
core.cn: 时间上前方不远处。

branches.en: A train light appears around the bend.
branches.cn: 拐弯处出现了火车的灯光。

branches.en: A guest rises before the meal ends.
branches.cn: 饭还没吃完，客人就起身了。

branches.en: A phone rings the moment a door opens.
branches.cn: 门一开，电话就响了。

branches.en: A short wait and an early start are neighbours.
branches.cn: 短暂的等待与提早出发是邻居。

branches.en: No delay is the shortest kind of soon.
branches.cn: 毫不耽搁，是最短的「不久」。

intro.en: Soon has a small family of comparative and fixed time phrases.
intro.cn: soon 有一小组比较级形式和固定时间短语。

latinIntro.en: Soon has no Latin root; it comes from Old English sona.
latinIntro.cn: soon 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 sona。

items.example: The soonest train leaves at six.
The doctor will see you presently.
items.exampleCN: 医生马上就会给你看诊。

definition_zh: 花费；价钱；成本；代价
definition_en: the money needed to buy or do something; to have a price
core_image: 收银台跳出的数字，付出去就不回来了
scene: 春游前大家讨论要不要租自行车环湖。 The bike hire will cost each of us twenty yuan.
sceneCN: 这里 cost 是动词「花费」（第 1 个义项：需要付出钱）；句意是租车每人要花二十元。

derivatives.zh: 由 cost 加 -ly 构成，义为「昂贵的」
义为「成本核算」

senses.title: To have a price
senses.definition: to have a particular price
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个价格
senses.example: This dictionary costs fifty yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 这本词典五十元。
senses.why: Cost is the constant: the price stands at what it stands.
senses.whyCN: cost 是恒定值：价格就停在那里。

senses.title: To make someone lose something valuable
senses.definition: to make someone lose money, time or something important
senses.definitionCN: 使某人失去钱、时间或重要之物
senses.example: The wrong turn cost us an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走错路让我们损失了一个小时。
senses.why: Money is only one thing the price can take; time and chances can also be paid.
senses.whyCN: 钱只是代价的一种；时间和机会同样可能被付出。

senses.title: The money needed for something
senses.definition: the amount of money needed to buy or do something
senses.definitionCN: 购买或做某事所需的钱数
senses.example: The total cost of the school trip is three hundred yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 学校春游的总费用是三百元。
senses.why: The noun names the number itself, the price tag.

intro.en: Cost began as a Latin word for standing together, then stood for a price.
intro.cn: cost 始于拉丁语「立于某处」，后来「站」出了价格。

items.en: The Latin verb constare meant to stand firm or to be fixed at, from com- (together) + stare (to stand).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 constare 意为坚定、定价为，由 com-（共同）+ stare（站立）构成。

items.en: Old French coster meant to cost, the price standing at a number.
items.cn: 古法语 coster 意为花费，价格立于某数。

items.en: English adopted cost in the thirteenth century for prices.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪吸收 cost，表示价格。

items.en: The noun grew senses for expenses and sacrifices.
items.cn: 名词衍生出费用与牺牲之义。

items.en: Business English added cost for production expenses.
items.cn: 商务英语又用 cost 指生产成本。

note.en: These words share the stare root of standing, or name expenses.
note.cn: 这些词共享 stare（站立）词根，或表示费用。

definition_zh: 单位；单元；部件；部队小单位；一元（计量的量）
definition_en: a single thing or group treated as one whole, especially in measuring or organizing
core_image: 一盒积木被分成一块一块，每块都算一个
scene: 装修师傅在图纸上把一间病房划成几个格子，每个格子单独计价。 The flat is divided into three units.
sceneCN: 这里 unit 是「单元」（第 1 个义项：被当作整体的一个部分）；句意为这套房子被分成三个单元。积木一块一块各算一个，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「联合；团结」
同根名词，义为「团结；统一」
同根形容词，义为「单一的；统一的」
同根动词，义为「统一；使一致」

senses.title: A single part counted as one
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a larger whole is divided for counting or planning
senses.definitionCN: 较大整体为计数或规划而划分出的一个部分
senses.example: The course is divided into twelve units.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课分成十二个单元。
senses.why: The root means one, so a unit is whatever is being counted as one.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「一」，因此 unit 就是被算作「一个」的那个东西。

senses.title: A fixed amount used in measuring
senses.definition: a standard quantity used to express measurements
senses.definitionCN: 用于表达测量结果的标准量
senses.example: The metre is a unit of length.
senses.exampleCN: 米是长度单位。
senses.why: Measuring means chopping a continuous thing into countable ones, and each piece is a unit.
senses.whyCN: 测量就是把连续的量切成可数的一个个，每一个就是 unit。

senses.title: A piece of equipment or furniture
senses.definition: one item of equipment, or a piece that forms part of a machine
senses.definitionCN: 一台设备，或构成机器一部分的组件
senses.example: The cooling unit needs replacing every three years.
senses.exampleCN: 冷却装置每三年要更换一次。
senses.why: Machines are built from countable one-pieces, and the pieces keep the name.
senses.whyCN: 机器由可数的「一个个」拼成，这些部件也沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: A small group in an organization
senses.definition: a group that works as one body, especially in an army or hospital
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个整体行动的小组，尤指军队或医院中的
senses.example: A medical unit was sent to the mountain village.
senses.exampleCN: 一支医疗队被派往那个山村。
senses.why: Several people acting as one are, from outside, a single unit.
senses.whyCN: 几个人如同一个人那样行动，从外面看就是一个 unit。

senses.title: A private flat or building section
senses.definition: one separate living space or workshop within a larger building
senses.definitionCN: 较大建筑内一个独立的居住空间或车间
senses.example: They rented a small unit above the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们租了车库上方的一个小单元。
senses.why: A building can be cut into countable spaces, each of which stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 一栋房子可以被切成一个个可数的空间，每个空间各自独立。

intro.en: The word is a contraction of the Latin word for one, first used in English by mathematicians.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「一」的缩略形式，最早由英语中的数学家用起来。

items.en: Unus meant one, and unitas meant oneness.
items.cn: unus 意为「一」，unitas 意为「一体」。

items.en: English writers formed unit from the Latin root for use in arithmetic.
items.cn: 十六世纪的作者用这个拉丁词根造出 unit，用于算术。

items.en: It spread from numbers to any single part counted as one.
items.cn: 它从数字扩展到任何被算作一个的部分。

items.en: Military and medical units gave it an organizational sense.
items.cn: 军队与医疗机构中的 unit 赋予了它组织层面的意义。

items.en: Housing units and industrial units bring it into everyday building language.
items.cn: 住房单元与工业厂房单元让它进入日常的建筑语言。

definition_zh: 不同意；意见不一致；有分歧
definition_en: to have a different opinion from someone
core_image: 两个人指着相反方向的箭头
scene: 小组讨论春游去哪，两个人意见不合。 I disagree with Tom: the museum is better than the park.
sceneCN: 这里 disagree 是「不同意」（第 1 个义项：意见不同）；句意是我不同意汤姆的看法：博物馆比公园更好。

senses.title: To have a different opinion
senses.definition: to have a different opinion from someone else
senses.definitionCN: 与别人看法不同
senses.example: Experts disagree about the best way to learn English.
senses.exampleCN: 专家们在学英语的最佳方法上意见不一。
senses.why: Agree comes from gratus (pleasing); dis- removes the pleasing, so disagree is to stop seeing eye to eye.
senses.whyCN: agree 出自 gratus（令人高兴的），加上 dis- 便失去了那份「合意」，即看法不再一致。

senses.title: To clash or not match
senses.definition: to be different from each other, or not to match
senses.definitionCN: 彼此不同或不相符
senses.example: The two reports disagree on the number of visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告在游客人数上不一致。
senses.why: When two accounts cannot please each other, they clash; the word moved from opinions to facts.
senses.whyCN: 两份说法无法「互相合意」，便相互冲突；词义从看法扩展到事实。

items.en: Disagreement names the state, disagreeable the unpleasant manner.

definition_en: the act of moving through the air, and any single instance, group, or path of such movement, including a set of stairs and the feathers that steady an arrow
core_image: 一只鸟从石阶底部掠起，沿着一道弧线飞过屋顶，翅尖的羽毛在光里闪了一下
scene: 清晨的山脊上，一群候鸟被光线的变化惊起，贴着坡面滑向另一侧谷地。 The flock rose into flight as the sun broke over the ridge.
sceneCN: 这里 flight 是「飞行」（第 1 个义项：在空中移动这一动作本身）；句意为太阳越过山脊时，鸟群起飞了。

senses.title: The Act of Flying
senses.definition: the action or process of moving through the air on wings or in an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 凭借翅膀或飞行器在空中移动的动作或过程
senses.example: The gulls' flight over the harbour lasted only a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥掠过港湾的飞行只持续了几秒钟。
senses.why: flyht is the bare action noun built on the verb fleogan 'to fly'; the suffix -t turns the doing into a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: flyht 是由动词 fleogan「飞」直接构成的动作名词，后缀 -t 把「做」变成可以命名的「事」。

senses.title: A Scheduled Air Journey
senses.definition: a trip made by air, especially one operated on a regular service between two places
senses.definitionCN: 乘飞机的一次行程，尤指两地间按班期运营的航次
senses.example: Our flight to Denver leaves before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 我们飞往丹佛的航班在黎明前起飞。
senses.why: a scheduled service is one completed act of flying, so the uncountable action is counted out into separate items.
senses.whyCN: 一次班期服务就是一整次完成的飞行，于是不可数的动作被切分成一个个可数的班次。

senses.title: A Flock on the Wing
senses.definition: a group of birds or aircraft moving through the air together
senses.definitionCN: 一起在空中移动的一群鸟或飞行器
senses.example: A flight of geese crossed the marsh at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 一群大雁在黄昏时飞越沼泽。
senses.why: the collective noun applies the action to the whole body that performs it at one time, so the group is named after its flight.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词把动作归给同时做出它的整个群体，于是这一群就以「飞行」命名。

senses.title: A Set of Stairs
senses.definition: a continuous run of steps between one floor or landing and the next
senses.definitionCN: 两层楼或两个平台之间连续的一串台阶
senses.example: She carried the box up the last flight of stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把箱子搬上了最后一段楼梯。
senses.why: a run of steps rises step after step like a body climbing through air, so English lent the word for flying to this rising series.
senses.whyCN: 一串台阶一级接一级地上升，像身体在空中爬升，英语于是把「飞行」这个词借给了这道上升的序列。

senses.title: Escape by Running
senses.definition: the act of fleeing or being driven away from danger
senses.definitionCN: 逃离危险或被赶离现场的行为
senses.example: The intruders were put to flight by a single shout.
senses.exampleCN: 一声喊叫就把闯入者赶跑了。
senses.why: fleeing is the oldest figurative use of flying: the body takes off as if on wings, so the same noun covers panic movement on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 逃跑是「飞」最古老的比喻用法：身体仿佛长了翅膀般离开，同一个名词因此也指地面上的仓皇移动。

senses.title: Path of a Projectile
senses.definition: the curved course followed by an arrow, bullet or ball through the air
senses.definitionCN: 箭、子弹或球在空中划出的弧线路径
senses.example: The arrow's flight flattened as it lost speed.
senses.exampleCN: 箭在速度衰减时，飞行弧线变得平缓。
senses.why: a projectile repeats the core action without wings: it too crosses the air along a line, and the line is named after the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 抛射体没有翅膀却重复了核心动作：它也沿一条线穿过空气，这条线就以「穿越」命名。

senses.title: Flight of Fancy
senses.definition: a burst of imaginative invention that has little grounding in fact
senses.definitionCN: 一段缺少事实依据的想象性发挥
senses.example: The plan was a flight of fancy that no budget could support.
senses.exampleCN: 那项计划纯属异想天开，没有哪份预算支撑得起。
senses.why: the mind is pictured as taking off and leaving the ground of fact, exactly the movement the word already names.
senses.whyCN: 这里把心智想象成起飞、离开事实的地面，正是这个词本已命名的那个动作。

senses.title: Feathers on an Arrow
senses.definition: the feathers fitted near the head of an arrow shaft to keep it steady in flight
senses.definitionCN: 装在箭杆尾端附近、使箭飞行稳定的羽毛
senses.example: He replaced the torn flight on the arrow before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前他换掉了箭上破损的箭羽。
senses.why: the feather is the part that makes the arrow fly straight, so the effect is named by the very act it serves.
senses.whyCN: 羽毛正是让箭飞得笔直的那一部分，于是这一部件用它服务的那个动作来命名。

intro.en: Flight comes straight from Old English flyht, an action noun made from the strong verb fleogan 'to fly' plus the suffix -t. The family is Germanic, not Latin.
intro.cn: flight 直接来自古英语 flyht，是由强动词 fleogan「飞」加后缀 -t 构成的动作名词；整个词族属日耳曼语，与拉丁语无关。

items.en: Fleogan was the everyday verb 'to fly', a strong verb of the second class, and it is the direct ancestor of modern fly.
items.cn: fleogan 是日常表示「飞」的动词，属第二类强动词，是现代 fly 的直接祖先。

items.en: Old English formed action nouns by adding -t to a verb stem, as in gift from giefan and weight from wegan; flyht follows the same pattern.
items.cn: 古英语在动词词干后加 -t 构成动作名词，如 gift 来自 giefan、weight 来自 wegan；flyht 遵循同一模式。

items.en: Flyht meant both the act of flying and a flying group, and it already carried the sense of fleeing from an enemy.
items.cn: flyht 既指飞行的动作，也指飞行的群体，并且已经带有「逃避敌人」的意思。

items.en: Middle English flight kept the noun while the verb became fly; the staircase sense appears in the record later, formed on the image of a rising run of steps.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了名词 flight，动词则演变为 fly；楼梯义在文献中出现较晚，建立在「一级级上升」的意象上。

items.en: German Flug 'flight' and Dutch vlucht are built from the same verb with the same suffix, which confirms the pattern rather than any Latin source.
items.cn: 德语 Flug「飞行」与荷兰语 vlucht 由同一动词加同一后缀构成，这证实了该构词模式，而非任何拉丁来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic only): the deeper Indo-European root behind fleogan is a reconstruction, and the arrow-feather sense has no firm first date.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅限日耳曼语之前）：fleogan 背后更早的印欧词根属重构形式，箭羽义的可靠首见年代亦不可考。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble flight in spelling or sound but mostly belong to other roots; group two holds the travel and airborne words that overlap with one or another of its senses.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音近似、但多数属于其他词根的词；第二组是在某个义项上与 flight 重叠的旅行与空中词汇。

entries.definition: Sudden fear; from Old English fyrhto, a noun of fear, with no connection to flying and no shared root with flight.
entries.definitionCN: 指突如其来的恐惧；来自古英语 fyrhto「恐惧」，与飞行无关，也与 flight 不同词根。

entries.definition: A group of ships, from Old English flēot, tied to flēotan 'to float'; the adjective fleet 'fast' is a separate Norse borrowing, so neither is kin to flight.
entries.definitionCN: 指船队，来自古英语 flēot，与 flēotan「漂浮」相关；形容词 fleet「快速」另从古诺斯语借入，二者都不是 flight 的同源词。

entries.definition: Built on flight plus -y, originally 'given to flight', hence fickle or frivolous; it shares the root but describes temperament.
entries.definitionCN: 由 flight 加 -y 构成，本义为「爱飞的」，引申为轻浮善变；词根相同，但描述的是性情。

entries.definition: To grow feathers fit for flight, from Old English -flycge 'fit to fly'; it belongs to the same flying family, though the exact link to fleogan is not settled.
entries.definitionCN: 指长出适合飞行的羽毛，来自古英语 -flycge「适合飞的」；属于同一「飞」词族，但它与 fleogan 的确切关系尚无定论。

entries.definition: A travel from one place to another by any means; flight is one kind of journey, limited to the air and to a single scheduled leg.
entries.definitionCN: 指以任何方式从一地到另一地的旅行；flight 是其中一种，限于空中且指单个航段。

entries.definition: A long journey, especially by sea or into space; it stresses distance and endurance rather than the act of flying.
entries.definitionCN: 指长途旅行，尤指海上或太空航行；强调距离与耐力，而非飞行动作。

entries.definition: To fly without flapping, riding rising air; it names one style of flight rather than flight as a category.
entries.definitionCN: 指不扇翅、借上升气流滑翔高飞；它命名的是飞行的一种方式，而非飞行这个类别。

entries.definition: The act of getting free from confinement or danger; it overlaps with flight in the sense of fleeing but says nothing about wings.
entries.definitionCN: 指摆脱拘禁或危险；在「逃跑」义上与 flight 重叠，但不含翅膀的意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real cognates and real idioms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同源词与真实习语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fleogan 'to fly' + -t: the act noun is built straight from the verb, exactly as gift is built on give.
normal.cn: fleogan「飞」+ -t：动作名词直接从动词构成，正如 gift 由 give 构成。

normal.en: German Flug and Dutch vlucht repeat the same verb-plus-suffix pattern, which fixes the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 德语 Flug 与荷兰语 vlucht 重复了同一套「动词加后缀」的模式，固定了这个词的形状。

normal.en: The staircase sense keeps the shape of the core image: a series climbing, step after step.
normal.cn: 楼梯义保留了核心意象的形状：一级接一级地向上攀升。

normal.en: put to flight means to make someone fly away, and take flight means to leave the ground or to run.
normal.cn: put to flight 意为使人飞逃，take flight 意为离地起飞或逃走。

normal.en: The family runs fly, flight, flighty, flightless, flighted.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fly、flight、flighty、flightless、flighted。

abstract.en: Picture a spiral staircase seen from above: each step is one beat of a wing.
abstract.cn: 想象从上方俯瞰一道螺旋楼梯：每一级台阶就是一次振翅。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow's feather slicing the air, correcting the shaft with every wobble.
abstract.cn: 想象箭尾的羽毛切开空气，每一次晃动都被它矫正。

abstract.en: Picture a line of geese at dusk, one continuous stroke drawn across the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时一列大雁，在天幕上画出一道连续的笔画。

examples.en: The engineer traced the flight of the ball with a slow-motion camera.
examples.cn: 工程师用慢动作摄影机追踪球的飞行轨迹。

examples.en: Bad weather forced the airline to cancel every flight before noon.
examples.cn: 恶劣天气迫使航空公司在中午前取消了所有航班。

examples.en: A flight of swallows passed low over the harvested field.
examples.cn: 一群燕子低低掠过收割后的田野。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「弗莱特」——像滑过天空的一道亮线，一掠而过 → 飞行；再想那段楼梯，也是一级级往上「飞」。

root: 古英语 flyht「飞行、飞行的群体」，由 fleogan「飞」（现代 fly 的祖先）+ 动作名词后缀 -t 构成，日耳曼语族，与德语 Flug、荷兰语 vlucht 同型；fleogan 更早的印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses hang on one movement: something leaves the ground and travels a line through air. Counting that movement gives a flight number, grouping it gives a flock, copying it on the ground gives stairs, fleeing gives escape, and the line it draws gives the trajectory and the feather that steadies it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都挂在同一个动作上：某物离地，在空中走出一条线。把这一动作计数，就有航班号；把做出它的群体归拢，就有鸟群；让它在土地上复制，就有楼梯；用它来逃离，就有逃跑；把那条线取下来，就有弹道，也有让箭沿线的箭羽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body leaving the ground and drawing a line through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体离地，在空中划出一道线。

branches.en: THE ACTION ITSELF: flying, then one finished act of it counted as a scheduled trip.
branches.cn: 动作本身：先有飞行，再把一次完成的飞行计作一个班次。

branches.en: WHAT CARRIES THE MOTION: the flock that flies and the feather that keeps the arrow flying true.
branches.cn: 承载动作之物：飞行的鸟群，以及让箭飞直的羽毛。

branches.en: RISING IN PLACE: a run of steps repeats the climb without any air.
branches.cn: 原地上升：一串台阶在没有空气的地方重复了攀爬。

branches.en: FLYING AWAY: panic turns the same noun into escape.
branches.cn: 飞离：惊慌把同一个名词变成逃跑。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: a projectile follows it literally, a daydream follows it in the mind.
branches.cn: 画出的线：抛射体在实处沿着它，白日梦在心上沿着它。

intro.en: Flight reads as two pieces: the Germanic verb stem for flying, and an old action-noun suffix. Everything else in the family is built by adding English endings to this noun.
intro.cn: flight 可以拆成两段：表「飞」的日耳曼动词词干，以及一个古老的动作名词后缀；词族中其余的词都是在这个名词上再加英语词尾构成的。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin entry to give: flight is Germanic throughout, and its cognates are German Flug and Dutch vlucht, not any Latin noun.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词形可列：flight 全程属日耳曼语，同源词是德语 Flug 与荷兰语 vlucht，而非任何拉丁名词。

items.structure: fleogan (Old English strong verb, class II)
items.meaning: to move through the air on wings
items.example: The stem supplies the bare act of flying.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供「飞」这一纯粹的动作。

items.structure: -t (Old English action-noun suffix, as in gift, weight)
items.meaning: the act or result of doing the verb
items.meaningCN: 动词所指动作或其结果
items.example: Add -t to the verb and the flying becomes a thing.
items.exampleCN: 在动词后加 -t，飞行就变成一件可以指称的事。

items.meaning: the act of flying; a flying group; a fleeing
items.example: Flight is recorded in Old English as flyht.
items.exampleCN: flight 在古英语中写作 flyht。

items.meaningCN: 爱飞的，引申为轻浮善变的
items.example: A flighty person is one whose attention keeps taking off.
items.exampleCN: flighty 的人，注意力总在起飞。

items.example: A flighted arrow carries its own stabiliser.
items.exampleCN: 装有箭羽的箭自带稳定器。

items.example: The suffix removes exactly the capacity the noun names.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀恰好去掉了名词所指的那种能力。

items.meaning: the route or line along which something flies
items.example: Controllers cleared the aircraft along a new flight path.
items.exampleCN: 管制员让这架飞机沿一条新飞行路线通行。

items.meaning: the cockpit, or the deck where aircraft take off
items.example: The flight deck is the part of the ship given to flying.
items.exampleCN: 飞行甲板是舰上专门交给飞行使用的那部分。

items.example: The missile was destroyed in flight.
items.exampleCN: 导弹在飞行途中被摧毁。

definition_zh: 庆祝；祝贺；歌颂；主持（仪式）
definition_en: to do something enjoyable to mark a special day or success, or to praise publicly
core_image: 一群人举杯欢呼，彩带从空中落下
scene: 球队赢下决赛那天，全班在教室里开了一场小小的庆祝会。 The whole class held a small party to celebrate the team's final win.
sceneCN: 这里 celebrate 是「庆祝」（第 1 个义项：以欢乐活动纪念好事）；句意为全班开小会庆祝球队夺冠。

pos.zh: 庆祝；祝贺；歌颂；主持仪式

derivatives.zh: 由 celebrate 加 -ion 构成，义为「庆祝；庆典」
同根词，义为「名人；名声」
由 celebrate 加 -ed 构成，义为「著名的；驰名的」

senses.title: To mark a happy event with joy
senses.definition: to take part in enjoyable activities for a special day or success
senses.definitionCN: 以欢乐活动纪念特殊日子或成功
senses.example: We celebrate Spring Festival with dumplings.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃饺子庆祝春节。
senses.why: Latin celebrare meant to visit often and honour in crowds, and honouring turns into partying.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 celebrare 指常去、聚众礼赞，礼赞渐变为欢庆。

senses.title: To praise someone or something
senses.definition: to praise publicly in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 以言语或文字公开赞美
senses.example: The poem celebrates the courage of the firefighters.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗讴歌消防员的勇气。
senses.why: To honour a thing repeatedly is to praise it, so the word kept that face too.
senses.whyCN: 反复礼赞即是称颂，这个词也保留了这一面。

senses.title: To perform a religious rite
senses.definition: to perform a ceremony, especially a religious one
senses.definitionCN: 主持典礼，尤指宗教仪式
senses.example: The priest celebrated Mass on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 神父周日主持弥撒。
senses.why: Crowd-honouring was first of all a public rite, and rites still need someone to lead.
senses.whyCN: 聚众礼赞本是公共仪式，仪式至今仍需主持之人。

intro.en: Celebrate goes back to a Latin word for honouring something in a crowd.
intro.cn: celebrate 上溯拉丁语「聚众礼赞」之词。

items.en: Latin celebrare meant to frequent, honour and perform in company.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celebrare 意为常至、礼赞、聚众而行。

items.en: Its root celebris described a place thronged with many people.
items.cn: 词根 celebris 形容「人头攒动」之地。

items.en: Old French celebrer kept the religious ceremony sense.
items.cn: 古法语 celebrer 保留宗教仪式义。

items.en: Middle English celebrate meant to perform rites and honour publicly.
items.cn: 中古英语 celebrate 兼指行礼与公开礼赞。

items.en: Modern English stressed joyful parties, praise and famous names.
items.cn: 现代英语强调欢庆、赞美与「名人」。

note.en: The first group collects same-root words; the second collects joy-and-praise words.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词，第二组收欢庆与赞美类词。

entries.definition: The act or party of celebrating.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「庆祝；庆典」，是其派生词。

entries.definition: A famous person.
Great speed, a rare formal word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迅速」，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: To remember a past event formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「纪念」，侧重回顾。

entries.definition: To speak well of.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「称赞」，与歌颂义相邻。

entries.definition: To keep a festival or custom.

normalIntro.en: Remember celebrate through its crowd-honouring root.
normalIntro.cn: 借「聚众礼赞」词根记忆 celebrate。

normal.en: celebrate comes from celebris, thronged with people.
normal.cn: celebrate 源自 celebris（人潮涌动）。

normal.en: celebrity is a person much celebrated.
normal.cn: celebrity 即被频频礼赞之人。

normal.en: celebration is the party itself.
normal.cn: celebration 是庆典本身。

normal.en: celebrated means famous.
normal.cn: celebrated 义为「著名的」。

normal.en: we celebrate wins, birthdays and festivals.
normal.cn: 胜利、生日与节日都要庆祝。

abstract.en: Hear confetti cannons burst at midnight.
abstract.cn: 听午夜彩带炮砰然炸响。

abstract.en: See the banner rise as the crowd cheers.
abstract.cn: 横幅升起，人群欢呼。

abstract.en: Feel hands clapping until they sting.
abstract.cn: 鼓掌鼓到手心发麻。

examples.en: They celebrated her birthday with a homemade cake.
examples.cn: 他们用自制蛋糕为她庆祝生日。

examples.en: The writer is celebrated for her short stories.
examples.cn: 这位作家以短篇小说闻名。

examples.en: Fireworks celebrated the city's founding day.
examples.cn: 焰火庆祝了这座城市的建城日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛了不雷」——赛完赢了，不雷不响怎么庆祝。

root: 拉丁语 celebris（拥挤的；著名的）→ celebrare（礼赞；举行）→ 古法语 celebrer → 英语 celebrate；同族 celebrity、celebration、celebrated。

sensesIntro.en: Celebrate moves from crowd-honouring rites to birthday cakes, poems and famous names.
sensesIntro.cn: celebrate 从聚众之礼走向生日蛋糕、诗篇与名望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands lifted together over one good thing
core.cn: 核心意象：为一件好事，无数只手同时举起

branches.en: Parties for happy days
branches.cn: 为好日子办的聚会

branches.en: Poems and speeches of praise
branches.cn: 诗与演说中的赞美

intro.cn: celebrate 的拉丁词根 celebr- 清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: From celebris the family grew parties, fame and praise.
latinIntro.cn: 从 celebris 长出欢庆、名望与赞美三支。
