definition_zh: 温度；体温；发烧；气温
definition_en: a measure of how hot or cold something is
core_image: 墙上的温度计里，红色液柱停在一个刻度上，室内外差出一大截
scene: 实验室墙上的温度计显示，室内比室外高许多。 The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「可测量的冷热程度」（第 1 个义项：温度读数）；句意为温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。

derivatives.zh: 调和；使缓和 / 脾气
温带的；有节制的
性情；气质
温度计
恒温器

senses.title: A measured degree of heat
senses.definition: a number expressing how hot or cold a body or space is
senses.definitionCN: 表示物体或空间冷热程度的数值
senses.example: The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'a tempering or moderation'; early science used it for the balance of hot and cold in a body, then for the measured balance itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「调和、适度」；早期科学用它指体内冷热的平衡，后来指被测出的这个平衡。

senses.title: Body heat
senses.definition: the internal heat of a living body, normally around thirty-seven degrees
senses.definitionCN: 活体内部的温度，正常约三十七度
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's temperature twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天记录病人两次体温。
senses.why: A living body regulates its own balance of heat, which is exactly what the old sense of tempering described.
senses.whyCN: 活体自行调节冷热平衡，这正是旧义「调和」所描述的。

senses.title: The weather figure
senses.definition: the outdoor air temperature reported in a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 预报中报告的室外空气温度
senses.example: The forecast gives a temperature of minus five tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 预报说今晚气温为零下五度。
senses.why: Air is a body too, and meteorology applies the same measurement to the atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 空气也是一种物体，气象学把同一测量用到大气上。

senses.title: A fever
senses.definition: an abnormally high body temperature caused by illness
senses.definitionCN: 疾病引起的异常升高的体温
senses.example: The child has a temperature and should stay home.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子发烧了，应该待在家里。
senses.why: In everyday speech a 'temperature' means the raised figure, not the normal one, so the measurement stands for the illness.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语中 a temperature 指升高的那个数值，而不是正常值，于是测量结果代表了疾病。

senses.title: A device set point
senses.definition: the target temperature set on a thermostat or oven
senses.definitionCN: 在恒温器或烤箱上设定的目标温度
senses.example: Set the temperature to two hundred degrees before baking.
senses.exampleCN: 烘烤前把温度设为两百度。
senses.why: A control dial turns the noun into an instruction: the temperature is what the machine is told to reach.
senses.whyCN: 控制旋钮把这个名词变成指令：温度是机器被要求达到的值。

senses.title: The emotional climate
senses.definition: the general mood or level of tension in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中的总体情绪或紧张程度
senses.example: The temperature of the debate rose after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 声明发布后，辩论的火气升高了。
senses.why: Social heat is read like physical heat: a room can become hot with anger.
senses.whyCN: 社会的热像物理的热一样被读取：一个房间可以因愤怒而变热。

senses.title: A physical quantity
senses.definition: in physics, a property measuring the average kinetic energy of particles
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中衡量粒子平均动能的属性
senses.example: The temperature of the gas rises as the piston compresses it.
senses.exampleCN: 活塞压缩气体时，气体温度升高。
senses.why: Physics narrows the everyday number to a precise property of a system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把日常数字收窄为系统的精确属性。

senses.title: A standard condition
senses.definition: the ordinary indoor heat at which materials and reactions are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较材料与反应时所用的通常室内温度
senses.example: Store the reagent at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 把试剂存放在室温下。
senses.why: Labs need a standard, so 'room temperature' becomes a fixed benchmark rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 实验室需要一个标准，于是「室温」成了固定基准而不是描述。

intro.en: Temperature comes from Latin temperatura 'a tempering, a due mixture'. The modern physical sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: temperature 出自拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当的混合」。现代物理义是后来的收窄。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Temperatura meant a mixing in due proportion, from temperare 'to mix, regulate, restrain'.
items.cn: temperatura 意为按适当比例混合，出自 temperare「混合、调节、节制」。

items.en: Temperare is related to tempus 'time, season', because mixing in the right measure was imagined as keeping to the right season.
items.cn: temperare 与 tempus「时间、季节」相关，因为「按正确比例混合」被想象为顺应正确的时令。

items.en: Medieval medicine used temperatura for the balanced mixture of humours in a body, and English borrowed it as temperature in this medical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪医学用 temperatura 指体内体液的有序混合，英语借入时也带这一医学义。

items.en: With the thermometer, the word shifted from a balance of qualities to a measurable degree of heat.
items.cn: 随着温度计的发明，这个词从「性质的平衡」转为「可测量的热度」。

items.en: Physics fixed temperature as a quantity, and everyday speech kept the special phrase 'have a temperature' for fever.
items.cn: 物理学把 temperature 固定为一个物理量，日常口语则保留 have a temperature 这一说法指发烧。

items.en: Room temperature and body temperature became standard benchmarks in labs, kitchens and clinics.
items.cn: 室温与体温成为实验室、厨房与诊所的标准基准。

note.en: Group one separates the temperament words from the temperature word; group two holds related measures and sensations.
note.cn: 第一组分辨 temperament 词族与 temperature 的区别；第二组是相关度量与感觉词。

entries.definition: A person's usual character; it comes from the same Latin root, where a balance of humours was thought to shape personality.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人惯常的性格；出自同一拉丁词根，古人认为体液平衡塑造性格。

entries.definition: To moderate or to become angry easily; the noun means a state of mind, not a degree of heat.
entries.definitionCN: 使缓和，或指容易发怒；名词指心境，而不是热度。

entries.definition: Relating to time or to the material world; it comes from tempus 'time', not from temperare.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间或世俗世界有关；出自 tempus「时间」，而非 temperare。

entries.definition: The energy transferred by a difference in temperature; heat is the cause, temperature is the measured result.
entries.definitionCN: 因温差而传递的能量；热是原因，温度是被测出的结果。

entries.definition: A raised body temperature caused by illness; it names the condition, while a temperature is just the reading.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病引起的体温升高；它指病况，而 temperature 只是读数。

entries.definition: The figure shown by an instrument; a temperature is one kind of reading.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器显示的数字；温度是读数的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin family is real, and the measuring instruments are real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁词族真实存在，测量仪器也都是真实复合词。

normal.en: temperature and temperament share temperare: one measures the body's heat, the other names the body's mix of moods.
normal.cn: temperature 与 temperament 共享 temperare：一个测身体的热，一个指身体性情的混合。

normal.en: thermometer = thermo- (heat) + -meter (measure), the instrument that reads a temperature.
normal.cn: thermometer = thermo-「热」+ -meter「测量」，读取温度的仪器。

normal.en: thermostat = thermo- + -stat (standing, holding), a device that holds a set temperature.
normal.cn: thermostat = thermo- + -stat「保持」，把温度保持在设定值的装置。

normal.en: room temperature is the standard phrase in recipes and lab protocols for ordinary indoor heat.
normal.cn: room temperature 是食谱与实验规程中表示通常室内温度的标准说法。

normal.en: to have a temperature means to be feverish, because the number has gone above normal.
normal.cn: have a temperature 指发烧，因为那个数字高出了正常值。

abstract.en: Abstractly, temperature is balance made countable: hot and cold are weighed against each other and turned into a number.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，temperature 是可数的平衡：冷与热相互权衡，变成一个数字。

abstract.en: The same number can describe a room, a body, a gas or the mood of a meeting.
abstract.cn: 同一个数字可以描述房间、身体、气体，也可以描述一场会议的气氛。

abstract.en: So temperature is not heat itself but heat made comparable.
abstract.cn: 所以 temperature 不是热本身，而是变得可比较的热。

examples.en: The temperature fell below zero before dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明前气温降到了零下。

examples.en: Keep the oven at a constant temperature.
examples.cn: 让烤箱保持恒温。

examples.en: Her temperature returned to normal after two days.
examples.cn: 两天后她的体温恢复正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「天不热」：天不热也有温度 → temperature 温度

root: 拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当混合」← temperare「混合、调节」，与 tempus「时间、季节」相关；十七世纪起经温度计的使用转为可测量的热度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measurable balance: a room, a body, the weather, a fever, a thermostat setting, a social mood, a physical quantity and a standard benchmark.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一个可测的平衡展开：房间、身体、天气、发烧、恒温设定、群体情绪、物理量，以及标准基准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hot and cold weighed against each other and read off as a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷与热相互权衡，被读成一个数字。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: everyday heat and the physicist's quantity are the same number at two levels of precision.
branches.cn: 测量：日常热度与物理学家的物理量，是同一数字的两种精度。

branches.en: THE BODY: normal warmth and illness-heat are one scale read above and below the usual line.
branches.cn: 身体：正常体温与病热，是同一条刻度在常线上下两侧的读数。

branches.en: THE AIR: a forecast figure and a lab benchmark both describe ordinary surroundings.
branches.cn: 空气：预报数字与实验室基准都在描述平常环境。

branches.en: CONTROL: a dial turns the noun into a target to be reached.
branches.cn: 控制：旋钮把这个名词变成一个要达到的目标。

branches.en: MOOD: a room heated by anger borrows the same thermometer.
branches.cn: 情绪：被愤怒加热的房间借用了同一支温度计。

intro.en: Temperature belongs to the Latin temperare family. English adds -ature for the noun, while Greek thermo- supplies the instruments.
intro.cn: temperature 属于拉丁 temperare 词族。英语加 -ature 构成名词，希腊语 thermo- 则提供仪器名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries below are the recorded ancestors of the family; tempus 'time' is included because temperare was built on the idea of the right season.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁条目是该词族有记录的祖先；列出 tempus「时间」，因为 temperare 建立在「合宜时令」的观念上。

items.meaningCN: 读取温度的仪器（thermo- 表示热，-meter 表示测量）
items.exampleCN: 温度计读数是三十八度。

items.meaning: a device that keeps a set temperature
items.meaningCN: 把温度保持在设定值的装置（-stat 表示保持）
items.example: The thermostat switches the heater off.

items.meaning: to moderate; also a state of mind
items.example: She tempered her criticism with praise.
The temperate zone has four seasons.

items.meaning: kept at a fixed heat by a device
items.example: The samples sit in a temperature-controlled room.

items.meaning: the ordinary indoor heat, used as a benchmark
items.meaningCN: 通常的室内温度，用作基准
items.example: Serve the cheese at room temperature.

items.meaning: the internal heat of a living body
items.example: Body temperature is lowest before dawn.

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, regulate

definition_zh: 每日的；日常的；每天；日报
definition_en: happening every day; every day; a newspaper printed every day
core_image: 太阳每天升起，事情每天照做
scene: 每天早上七点半，宿舍楼下的小卖部都挤满买早餐的学生。 Brushing teeth is part of my daily morning plan.
sceneCN: 这里 daily 是「日常的」（第 1 个义项：每天都发生的）；句意是刷牙是我每天早晨计划的一部分。

derivatives.zh: daily 的基础词，义为「天；日」
由 day 加 light 构成，义为「日光；白天」

senses.title: Happening every day
senses.definition: happening or done once a day, or on every ordinary day
senses.definitionCN: 一天一次，或每个平常日子都会发生的
senses.example: Keeping a daily reading log helps me remember new words.
senses.exampleCN: 坚持每天记录阅读清单帮我记住新单词。
senses.why: Day names the unit of time; adding -ly turns the unit into an adjective about the unit.
senses.whyCN: day 是时间单位，加 -ly 后缀就把单位变成了描述它的形容词。

senses.title: Every day as an adverb
senses.definition: once each day, without missing a day
senses.definitionCN: 每天一次，一天不落
senses.example: The milk truck comes daily before six.
senses.exampleCN: 送奶车每天六点前来。
senses.why: The same suffix works twice: day by day becomes one word for each day.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀用两次，「一天又一天」缩成一个词，就是每天。

senses.title: A newspaper printed every day
senses.definition: a newspaper printed and sold every day
senses.definitionCN: 每天印刷发行的报纸
senses.example: Grandpa reads the daily over breakfast every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷每天早餐时读日报。
senses.why: A thing named by its schedule takes the schedule's word.
senses.whyCN: 按日程命名的事物便借用日程的词。

intro.en: Daily is simply day with an adjective ending.
intro.cn: daily 就是 day 加上形容词词尾。

items.en: dæg meant the period from sunrise to sunrise, our day.
items.cn: 古英语 dæg 指从日出到日出的时段，即一天。

items.en: The form dæglic already meant happening each day.
items.cn: 古英语形式 dæglic 已表示每天发生的。

items.en: Spelling settled as daily, keeping both adjective and adverb uses.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 daily，兼作形容词和副词。

items.en: With printing, daily became a noun for a newspaper issued every day.
items.cn: 印刷术兴起后，daily 又成为名词，指每天发行的报纸。

items.en: Today daily life, daily news and take the stairs daily are all common.
items.cn: 如今 daily life、daily news 和「每天走楼梯」都很常用。

note.en: These words belong to the day family or describe time rhythms.
note.cn: 这些词属于 day 词族，或描述时间节律。

entries.definition: a period of twenty-four hours
light from the sun during the day
milk products or a milk shop; spelled close to daily, unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 乳制品；奶店（拼写近似，词义无关）

entries.definition: a small white flower; its old name meant day's eye
entries.definitionCN: 雏菊（古义为「白昼之眼」，与 day 同源）

entries.definition: ordinary, happening commonly
happening every week
happening every month
happening at even intervals
happening every night

normalIntro.en: Build the word from day and compare the -ly time words.
normalIntro.cn: 从 day 出发拼词，并对比一组时间 -ly 词。

normal.en: day + ly = daily, one l plus y.
normal.cn: day + ly ＝ daily，一个 l 加 y。

normal.en: weekly, monthly, yearly follow the same pattern.
normal.cn: weekly（每周）、monthly（每月）、yearly（每年）同构。

normal.en: daily is both adjective and adverb: daily exercise, exercise daily.
normal.cn: daily 可作形容词和副词：daily exercise、exercise daily。

normal.en: A daily is also a newspaper printed every day.
normal.cn: daily 还可作名词，指每天出版的报纸。

normal.en: Watch out for dairy, the milk shop; one letter apart.
normal.cn: 小心别和 dairy（奶制品店）弄混，只差一个字母。

abstract.en: Picture the sun rising on schedule every single morning.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳每天准点升起。

abstract.en: Hear the same alarm at the same minute, day after day.
abstract.cn: 听每天同一分钟的同一个闹钟。

abstract.en: Feel the small tick of a calendar square being crossed out.
abstract.cn: 体会日历上格子被划掉的小小仪式感。

examples.en: Our daily walk to school takes ten minutes.
examples.cn: 我们每天步行上学要十分钟。

examples.en: Water the plant daily or it will dry out.
examples.cn: 这盆植物要每天浇水，不然会干枯。

examples.en: The school daily reports football results every Friday.
examples.cn: 学校日报每周五报道足球比赛结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得累」——每天都做的事，天天「得累」，所以是日常的

root: 来自古英语 dæg（天）加形容词后缀 -lic，dæglic 本指「每天的」；中古英语定型为 daily，兼作形容词与副词，近代又转指日报。

sensesIntro.en: The word fills one rhythm: once a day, day after day.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词只填一种节律：一天一次，天天如此。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun rising again, so the same things repeat
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳照常升起，事情天天重演

branches.en: Daily life and daily tasks
branches.cn: 日常生活与每日任务

branches.en: Doing something once each day
branches.cn: 每天做一次某事

branches.en: The morning newspaper
branches.cn: 早晨的报纸

branches.en: Adjective and adverb of one rhythm
branches.cn: 同一节律的形容词与副词

branches.en: Compared with weekly and monthly
branches.cn: 与 weekly、monthly 对照

intro.en: Daily shows the -ly pattern used for time words.
intro.cn: daily 展示了 -ly 用在时间词上的构词法。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the family is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，词族来自古英语。

items.exampleCN: a yearly trip（一年一次的旅行）

items.meaning: milk products; spelled near daily, unrelated
items.meaningCN: 乳制品（拼写近似，词义无关）

definition_zh: 冠军；优胜者；拥护者；捍卫者；为……而战；支持
definition_en: a person or team that wins first place; someone who defends a cause; to support strongly
core_image: 领奖台上举起奖杯的第一名，或为一个目标挺身而出的人
scene: 全校运动会的领奖台上，我们班的长跑冠军高高举起了奖杯。 Our class runner became the school champion in the 800-metre race.
sceneCN: 这里 champion 是「冠军」（第 1 个义项：比赛获得第一名的人）；句意为我们班的运动员成为校运会八百米冠军。

collocations.zh: 为事业奔走；支持一项事业

derivatives.zh: 由 champion 加 -ship 构成，义为「锦标赛；冠军地位」
由 champion 加后缀构成，义为「没有冠军的」

senses.title: The winner of first place in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that wins first place in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中获得第一名的人或队伍
senses.example: She is the school swimming champion this year.
senses.exampleCN: 她是今年的校游泳冠军。
senses.why: The one who fights for another side, and wins, naturally becomes the named victor of the field.
senses.whyCN: 替一方出战并获胜的人，自然就成了赛场上被命名的胜者。

senses.title: A person who fights or speaks for a cause
senses.definition: someone who strongly supports and defends a person, idea or group
senses.definitionCN: 坚定支持并捍卫某人、某想法或某团体的人
senses.example: He is a champion of cleaner rivers in our city.
senses.exampleCN: 他是本市洁净河流的坚定捍卫者。
senses.why: The word's oldest meaning was a fighter who took your place in battle, so any brave defender keeps this name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的含义是替你上阵的战士，因此一切勇敢的捍卫者都保留了这个名字。

senses.title: To support or defend publicly
senses.definition: to publicly support a cause, person or plan
senses.definitionCN: 公开支持某项事业、某人或某个计划
senses.example: The student union championed the plan for a reading corner.
senses.exampleCN: 学生会大力支持设立读书角的想法。
senses.why: When the defender keeps fighting for a cause, the fighter's name becomes a verb of supporting it.
senses.whyCN: 捍卫者持续为某项事业而战，战士之名便转成支持该事业的动词。

senses.title: A title or award for winning
senses.definition: the title given to the winner of a championship
senses.definitionCN: 授予锦标赛获胜者的称号
senses.example: The team held the champion title for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍连续三年保持冠军称号。
senses.why: The winner's name itself can stand for the prize and title attached to the win.
senses.whyCN: 胜者的名字本身也可以代指胜利带来的奖赏与头衔。

intro.en: Champion goes back to a Late Latin word for a battlefield fighter, reaching English through Old French.
intro.cn: champion 可追溯到晚期拉丁语中指「战场战士」的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Late Latin campio meant a fighter or duelist, built on campus, a field of battle.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 campio 指战士或决斗者，源于 campus（战场、原野）。

items.en: Old French champion meant a champion or defender, one who fights for another.
items.cn: 古法语 champion 指冠军或捍卫者，即替人出战之人。

items.en: Middle English took champion for a fighter in single combat or a defender.
items.cn: 中古英语用 champion 指单挑的斗士或捍卫者。

items.en: The sense narrowed to a winner in contests and games.
items.cn: 词义收窄，专指比赛中的获胜者。

items.en: Today champion names first-place winners, loyal defenders, and the act of supporting.
items.cn: 今天 champion 既指第一名、捍卫者，也指支持的行动。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects winners and supporters.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收优胜者与支持者类词。

entries.definition: A contest to find a champion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「锦标赛」，由 champion 派生。

entries.definition: A French sparkling wine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「香槟酒」，读音与 champion 相近。

entries.definition: A planned series of activities for a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运动；战役」，拼写与 champion 相近。

entries.definition: The person who wins a game or race.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获胜者」，与 champion 的冠军义相近。

entries.definition: Someone who wins a medal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奖牌获得者」，与 champion 相近。

entries.definition: A person who protects something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「捍卫者」，与 champion 的拥护义相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember champion by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 champion。

normal.en: the root is Latin campus, a battle field.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语 campus（战场）。

normal.en: championship is the contest or the title of a champion.
normal.cn: championship 指锦标赛或冠军身份。

normal.en: camp and champion share the field idea.
normal.cn: camp 与 champion 共享「场地」的概念。

normal.en: a champion of a cause is its brave defender.
normal.cn: 某项事业的 champion 就是它的勇敢捍卫者。

normal.en: champion as a verb means to support publicly.
normal.cn: champion 作动词意为公开支持。

abstract.en: Picture a trophy raised high under the crowd's roar.
abstract.cn: 想象奖杯在人群的欢呼声中被高高举起。

abstract.en: Hear your name called as the last flag is crossed.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见冲过终点旗时自己名字被念响。

abstract.en: Feel the steady heart of someone guarding a cause alone.
abstract.cn: 感受一个人独自守护某项事业时那颗坚定的心。

examples.en: Our class runner became the school champion in the 800-metre race.
examples.cn: 我们班的运动员成为校运会八百米冠军。

examples.en: She is a champion of animal rights in our school.
examples.cn: 她是学校里动物权益的坚定捍卫者。

examples.en: The students championed the idea of a school garden.
examples.cn: 学生们大力支持建校园花园的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抢瓶」——抢先抢到奖瓶的人就是冠军。

root: 拉丁语 campus（战场、原野）→ 晚期拉丁语 campio（战士）→ 古法语 champion → 现代英语 champion；同根词有 camp（营地）、campaign（战役、运动）。

sensesIntro.en: Champion moves from a battlefield fighter to a contest winner and a defender of causes.
sensesIntro.cn: champion 由战场战士转为比赛优胜者，再到事业的捍卫者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the fighter who stands first on the field
core.cn: 核心意象：战场上站到最前面的战士

branches.en: The first-place winner
branches.cn: 获得第一名的人

branches.en: A defender of a cause
branches.cn: 事业的捍卫者

branches.en: Publicly supporting something
branches.cn: 公开支持某事

branches.en: The champion's title
branches.cn: 冠军头衔

branches.en: Sports contest winners
branches.cn: 体育比赛的胜者

intro.en: Champion keeps the Latin field root camp- inside its spelling.
intro.cn: champion 的拼写中保留了拉丁语「场地」词根 camp-。

latinIntro.en: The root campus also gives English words for open ground and campaigns.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 campus 还给英语带来开阔场地与运动战役相关的词。

items.example: The champion fought on the field.

items.meaning: a place with tents or huts
items.example: We set up camp by the lake.

items.meaning: a planned effort or military operation
items.exampleCN: 他们开展了一场读书活动。

items.meaning: a contest for the champion title
the grounds of a school or university
items.example: The library is at the campus centre.
The league ended championless that year.
The scouts encamped in the forest.
He championed the cause of free libraries.
items.exampleCN: 他为免费图书馆的事业奔走。

definition_zh: 不同；差异；差额；分歧
definition_en: the way in which people or things are not the same
core_image: 并排的两样东西之间那道看不见的缝
scene: 科学课上我们比较了两个杯子的水温。 There is a small difference in temperature between the two cups.
sceneCN: 这里 difference 是「差异」（第 1 个义项：不一样的程度）；句意是两个杯子之间的水温略有差异。

derivatives.zh: difference 的形容词形式，义为「不同的」
由拉丁词根 differ 派生的动词，义为「不同；相异」
由 different 加 -ly 构成，义为「不同地」

senses.title: The way things are not the same
senses.definition: the quality or amount of being unlike
senses.definitionCN: 不一样的地方或程度
senses.example: The difference between the twins is easy to see now.
senses.exampleCN: 如今这对双胞胎的差异一眼就能看出。
senses.why: When two things stand apart, the gap between them gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西分开站着，它们之间的缝隙需要名字，这便是差异。

senses.title: The amount left after subtracting
senses.definition: the number that remains when one number is taken from another
senses.definitionCN: 一个数减去另一个数所得的结果
senses.example: The difference between nine and four is five.
senses.exampleCN: 九减四的差是五。
senses.why: Numbers also stand apart, and the distance between them is the gap.
senses.whyCN: 数字之间也有距离，两者相减留下的便是「差」。

senses.title: A disagreement
senses.definition: a disagreement between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间的意见不合
senses.example: Good friends can settle their differences with a talk.
senses.exampleCN: 好朋友能通过谈话化解分歧。
senses.why: Minds that stand apart create a gap of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 意见相左如同两颗心站开了距离，分歧便是想法间的缝。

intro.en: Difference comes from Latin words for carrying apart.
intro.cn: difference 来自拉丁语中表示「分开携带」的词。

items.en: Differre meant to carry apart, from dis- plus ferre (to carry).
items.cn: 拉丁语 differre 意为分开携带，由 dis- 加 ferre（搬运）构成。

items.en: Differentia named the quality of being unlike.
items.cn: differentia 指不相同这一性质。

items.en: Old French difference carried it into learned writing.
items.cn: 古法语 difference 把它带入书面语。

items.en: English took difference in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 difference。

items.en: Maths fixed the subtraction sense, and daily speech added the disagreement sense.
items.cn: 数学固定了差数义，日常用语增添了分歧义。

note.en: These words share the carrying-apart root or describe gaps.
note.cn: 这些词与「分开携带」词根同源，或同样描述差距。

entries.definition: not the same
to be unlike
in another way
hard to do, different root
entries.definitionCN: 困难的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a meeting, from ferre
entries.definitionCN: 会议（同含 ferre 词根）

entries.definition: a clear difference
a space between
the way things are alike
a disagreement in words
many kinds

normalIntro.en: Use the gap image and the ferre family to remember difference.
normalIntro.cn: 用「缝隙」的画面和 ferre 词族记住 difference。

normal.en: the difference between two things is the gap.
normal.cn: the difference between 表示两者间的差距。

normal.en: make a difference means change something.
normal.cn: make a difference 表示带来改变。

normal.en: in maths, difference is the answer to subtraction.
normal.cn: 数学中 difference 指减法的差。

normal.en: different is the adjective; difference is the noun.
normal.cn: different 是形容词，difference 是名词。

normal.en: one c, one f in the middle: dif-fer-ence.
normal.cn: 中间是 dif-fer-ence 的拼法。

abstract.en: Picture two lines drawn slightly apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两条微微分开的线。

abstract.en: Feel the small click when you finally spot the change.
abstract.cn: 体会终于发现变化时的轻轻一悟。

abstract.en: Hear friends laughing about their small disagreements.
abstract.cn: 听朋友们笑着聊彼此的小分歧。

examples.en: What is the difference between a rabbit and a hare?
examples.cn: 家兔和野兔有什么区别？

examples.en: One kind word can make a big difference to a sad friend.
examples.cn: 一句暖心的话能让难过的朋友大为改观。

examples.en: Our team won by a difference of two points.
examples.cn: 我们队以两分之差获胜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「低幅润丝」——低幅两幅画，润色几丝，看出「差异」

root: 来自拉丁语 differentia（不同之处），词根 differre 意为「分开携带」，由 dis-（分离）加 ferre（搬运）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Difference names the gap between things, numbers and minds.
sensesIntro.cn: difference 既指事物之差，也指数目之差与意见之别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the gap between two things
core.cn: 核心意象：两物之间的那道缝

branches.en: Spotting what is unlike
branches.cn: 发现不同之处

branches.en: Subtraction's answer
branches.cn: 减法的答案

branches.en: Opinions standing apart
branches.cn: 站开的意见

branches.en: Gap seen and gap counted
branches.cn: 看得见的差与算得出的差

branches.en: Talks can close the gap
branches.cn: 谈话能弥合差距

intro.en: Difference is built on the Latin root for carrying apart.
intro.cn: difference 建立在拉丁语「分开携带」词根上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root fer means to carry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 fer 意为搬运。

definition_zh: 主要的；最重要的；主管道；总线路；市电；大海
definition_en: most important or largest; a principal pipe or cable for water, gas or electricity; the public power supply; the open sea
core_image: 一张地图上，最粗的那条路通向城市中心
scene: 暴雪过后的清晨，维修车沿着城外最宽的那条公路往城里开。 The main road into the valley was still blocked by snow.
sceneCN: 这里指最重要、最主要的那条（第 1 个义项：主要的）；句意为通往山谷的主路仍被雪堵住。

pos.zh: 主管道；总线路；市电；大海

derivatives.zh: 由 main 加 -ly 构成，义为「主要地；大部分地」
由 main 与 land 复合，义为「大陆；本土」
由 main 与 stream 复合，义为「主流」
由 main 与 stay 复合，义为「支柱；主要依靠」

senses.title: Most important or largest
senses.definition: being the most important, largest or most influential of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类别中最重要、最大或最有影响力的
senses.example: The main reason for the delay was the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的主要原因是天气。
senses.why: Old English mægen meant strength, so what is main is what carries the greatest weight in a situation.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mægen 意为力量，因此 main 指在某个局面里分量最重的那一个。

senses.title: A principal pipe or cable
senses.definition: the largest pipe or cable that carries water, gas or electricity to many places
senses.definitionCN: 把水、燃气或电输送到许多地方的最大管道或线路
senses.example: A burst water main flooded the lower street.
senses.exampleCN: 一根爆裂的自来水主管淹没了地势较低的那条街。
senses.why: The adjective naming the chief thing became a noun for the chief channel, because that pipe carries the greatest volume and serves the whole network.
senses.whyCN: 形容「主要之物」的形容词转成名词，指最主要的输送通道，因为那根管道输送量最大、服务整个网络。

senses.title: The open sea
senses.definition: the open ocean, especially when seen as a great expanse away from land
senses.definitionCN: 开阔的海洋，尤指远离陆地、显得辽阔无边的海面
senses.example: The ship sailed out into the main at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船在黎明时驶向外海。
senses.why: The old sense of main as great or mighty survived at sea, where the open ocean is the great expanse beyond the shore.
senses.whyCN: main 古义「宏大、强大」在海上留存下来：岸边之外那一片开阔水域就是宏大的存在。

senses.title: The public electricity supply
senses.definition: the ordinary electricity supply provided to homes and buildings, especially in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 供给住宅和建筑的常规电力，尤见于英式用法
senses.example: The lamp can run on batteries or on the mains.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯可以用电池，也可以接市电。
senses.why: British speakers call the shared public supply the mains because it is the central source every building draws from, like the main pipe of a water system.
senses.whyCN: 英式说法把公共供电称作 the mains，因为它是每栋建筑都从中取电的中心来源，就像供水系统里的主管道。

intro.en: Main comes from a Germanic noun for strength; the adjective for the strongest or chief thing later became a noun for the chief channel.
intro.cn: main 来自日耳曼语中表示力量的名词；表示最强、首要之物的形容词后来转成指主要通道的名词。

items.en: The adjective comes from mægen, a noun meaning power, strength or force.
items.cn: 这个形容词来自 mægen，一个意为力量、力气、威力的名词。

items.en: The reconstructed base *maginam carried the same idea of strength and ability, and it also lies behind might and may.
items.cn: 重构词根 *maginam 同样表示力量与能力，might 与 may 也出自这里。

items.en: Middle English main kept the sense of chief or principal, and the word began to describe the leading road, pipe or clause.
items.cn: 中古英语 main 保留「首要、主要」的意思，并开始用来描述最主要的道路、管道或从句。

items.en: The noun main narrowed to the principal channel of a water or gas system, while the sea sense remained poetic.
items.cn: 名词 main 缩小为供水或燃气系统的主管道，而「大海」义仍带诗意。

items.en: Modern British usage adds the mains for public electricity, and 「main road」, 「main idea」 and 「main clause」 fix the adjective in daily speech.
items.cn: 现代英式用法又用 the mains 指公共供电，「main road」「main idea」「main clause」则把形容词固定在日常表达里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on main or on its Germanic root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what ranks first.
note.cn: 形近组收由 main 或其日耳曼词根构成的词；近义组收表示排在最前的形容词。

entries.definition: Chiefly, or for the most part.
The principal land mass, as opposed to islands.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于岛屿而言的主要陆地；大陆。

entries.definition: The ideas or practices accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被多数人接受的思想或做法；主流。

entries.definition: The person or thing that provides the chief support.
entries.definitionCN: 提供主要支撑的人或事物；支柱。

entries.definition: Most important; the leader of a group.
First in importance; the head of a school.
Most important or most successful.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要或最成功的；领先的。

entries.definition: First in order or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 在顺序或重要性上居首的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from strength, becomes an adjective for what weighs most, and then a noun for the biggest pipe or supply.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从力量出发，先成为指「分量最重」的形容词，再成为指最大管道或供应的名词。

normal.en: Main comes from mægen, strength, so the main thing is the one with the most force behind it.
normal.cn: main 来自 mægen（力量），所以最主要的东西就是背后力量最大的那一个。

normal.en: The same root gives might and may, which still carry the idea of power and possibility.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 might 与 may，它们仍带着力量与可能性的意思。

normal.en: A water main is simply the main pipe, the adjective turned into a noun by dropping the word it described.
normal.cn: water main 就是「主要的管道」，形容词通过省去所修饰的词而变成名词。

normal.en: The mains in British homes is the shared public supply, the central channel that every socket draws from.
normal.cn: 英国家庭说的 the mains 是公共供电，是每个插座都从中取电的中心线路。

normal.en: Main clause and main idea show the adjective doing the same job in grammar and in thought: picking out what carries the weight.
normal.cn: main clause 与 main idea 表明这个形容词在语法和思想里做同一件事：挑出承载重量的部分。

abstract.en: The thickest road on a map is not always the longest, but it is the one the whole region depends on.
abstract.cn: 地图上最粗的那条路未必最长，却是整个地区依赖的那一条。

abstract.en: A single pipe under the street feeds every tap in the block; that hidden centrality is the word's quiet image.
abstract.cn: 街道下的一根管道养活整片街区的每个水龙头；这种看不见的中心性正是这个词安静的意象。

abstract.en: To call something main is to make a judgment about weight, not about size alone.
abstract.cn: 把某物称作 main，是在判断它的分量，而不只是判断它的体积。

examples.en: The main road into the valley was still blocked by snow.
examples.cn: 通往山谷的主路仍被雪堵住。

examples.en: A burst water main flooded the lower street.
examples.cn: 一根爆裂的自来水主管淹没了地势较低的那条街。

examples.en: The ship sailed out into the main at dawn.
examples.cn: 船在黎明时驶向外海。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门」——进城的大门那条路最重要；记住 main 是主要的、主路。

root: 古英语 mægen（力量）经中古英语 main（首要的）而来；同族词 might、may 也出自表示「力量、能力」的日耳曼词根，无可靠拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is greatest weight; from it come the principal channel, the public supply, and the old poetic sense of the open sea.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是分量最重；主要通道、公共供电，以及「大海」的古老诗意都由它分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the thickest road on a map, with every side road branching off it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上最粗的那条路，所有岔路都从它分出去。

branches.en: the widest road on a hand-drawn map
branches.cn: 手绘地图上最宽的那条路

branches.en: a buried pipe feeding every tap on the street
branches.cn: 埋在地下、供养整条街水龙头的管道

branches.en: a ship alone on a wide grey sea
branches.cn: 一艘船独自在灰色辽阔的海面上

branches.en: a lamp switched from battery to wall current
branches.cn: 一盏灯从电池切换到墙上的电流

branches.en: one adjective becoming a noun for the chief channel
branches.cn: 同一个形容词变成指主要通道的名词

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English noun of strength, its adjective use, and English compounds that extend the idea of the chief part.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语表示力量的名词、它的形容词用法，以及延伸「主要部分」之意的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its relatives are Germanic, such as might and may.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它的近亲属于日耳曼语，例如 might 与 may。

definition_zh: 休息；剩余部分；依靠；停止
definition_en: to relax, the part that remains, or to be supported by something
core_image: 一个人放下工具，靠在树边歇一口气
scene: 走了很远之后，大家在树荫下休息。 After a long walk, everyone rested in the shade.
sceneCN: 这里 rested 是 rest 的过去式，表示「休息」（第 2 个义项：停止活动以恢复体力）；句意：走了很远之后，大家在树荫下休息。

derivatives.zh: 宁静的；让人休息的
坐立不安的
宁静地

senses.title: The part that remains
senses.definition: the people or things that are left after the others are taken
senses.definitionCN: 其他人或事物被拿走之后剩下的部分
senses.example: I ate one apple and kept the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 我吃了一个苹果，把其余的留着。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different root meaning to remain, and it names what is left behind.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个意为「留下」的词根，指被留下的东西。

senses.title: A period of relaxation
senses.definition: a period of time spent relaxing or not working
senses.definitionCN: 用于放松或不工作的一段时间
senses.example: You look tired and need a good rest.
senses.exampleCN: 你看起来很累，需要好好休息。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is bodily rest, a pause from effort.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的英语义项是身体休息，即从劳作中暂停。

senses.title: To relax or stop activity
senses.definition: to stop working or moving in order to recover
senses.definitionCN: 停止工作或移动以恢复体力
senses.example: Let us rest here for a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在这里休息几分钟吧。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun of relaxation into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「休息」这一名词转化为动作。

senses.title: To be supported or based on
senses.definition: to be supported by something or to depend on it
senses.definitionCN: 由某物支撑或依赖某物
senses.example: The whole plan rests on one assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划建立在一个假设之上。
senses.why: Something at rest on a support is held up by it, which gives the sense of depending.
senses.whyCN: 静止在某支撑物上的东西由它托住，因此产生「依赖」的含义。

intro.en: Rest has two sources: Old English ræst, a pause from work, and Old French reste, from Latin restare, to remain.
intro.cn: rest 有两个来源：古英语 ræst（停工歇息）与古法语 reste（源自拉丁语 restare，留下）。

items.en: Ræst means a pause, sleep, or resting place.
items.cn: ræst 意为暂停、睡眠或休息之处。

items.en: Restare means to remain or stand back.
items.cn: restare 意为留下、留在后面。

items.en: Reste means the remainder.
items.cn: reste 意为剩余部分。

items.en: Rest carries both the pause and the remainder senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 rest 同时带有「休息」与「剩余」两种含义。

items.en: Modern English adds rest on, meaning to depend on.
items.cn: 现代英语增加 rest on，表示依赖。

note.en: Rest is a double-rooted word, close to its restful and restless family and to words for breaks and remainders.
note.cn: rest 是双词源词，与 restful、restless 词族以及表示休息和剩余的词相邻。

entries.definition: peaceful and relaxing
unable to stay still
relaxing or lying still
a short pause from work
the part that is left
to become less tense

normalIntro.en: Rest is two words in one coat: the pause from work and the part left over.
normalIntro.cn: rest 是穿着同一件外衣的两个词：从工作中暂停，以及剩下的部分。

normal.en: Take a rest means stop and relax for a while.
normal.cn: take a rest 表示停下来放松一会儿。

normal.en: The rest of the cake is in the fridge.
normal.cn: 剩下的蛋糕在冰箱里。

normal.en: A plan can rest on a single assumption.
normal.cn: 一个计划可能只建立在一个假设上。

normal.en: Restful places help you sleep well.
normal.cn: 宁静的地方有助于睡好。

normal.en: Compare break: a break is shorter, rest can be a longer state.
normal.cn: 对比 break：break 更短，rest 可以是更长的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a traveler setting down a heavy pack.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人放下沉重的背包。

abstract.en: Imagine a spoon resting across the rim of a cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子横搁在杯沿上。

abstract.en: Think of the last slice left on a plate.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子里剩下的最后一片。

examples.en: We walked for hours and then rested by the river.
examples.cn: 我们走了几个小时，然后在河边休息。

examples.en: She read the first page and skipped the rest.
examples.cn: 她读了第一页，其余部分跳过了。

examples.en: The argument rests on weak evidence.
examples.cn: 这个论点建立在薄弱的证据上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rest」——像人「靠」在椅子上歇一歇，也是剩下的部分；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ræst（歇息）＋ 古法语 reste（剩余，源自拉丁语 restare「留下」）→ 英语 rest，一身兼有「休息」与「剩余」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Rest first names what remains, then a pause for recovery, then the act of relaxing, and finally being supported by something.
sensesIntro.cn: rest 先指剩余之物，再指恢复体力的暂停，再指放松的动作，最后指由某物支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy pack set down and a body leaning back.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的背包被放下，身体向后靠。

branches.en: The remainder comes from the Latin remain root.
branches.cn: 剩余部分来自拉丁语「留下」词根。

branches.en: A pause for recovery comes from the Old English root.
branches.cn: 恢复体力的暂停来自古英语词根。

branches.en: The verb of relaxing turns the pause into action.
branches.cn: 休息的动词把暂停变为动作。

branches.en: Being supported links rest to reliance.
branches.cn: 被支撑把 rest 与依赖联系起来。

branches.en: Something at rest lies supported and still.
branches.cn: 静止之物躺在那儿，被支撑着不动。

intro.en: Rest has two roots, and its English family grows with -ful, -less, and -ing.
intro.cn: rest 有两个词根，其英语词族由 -ful、-less 与 -ing 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin restare means to remain, from re-, back, and stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 restare 意为留下，由 re-（向后）与 stare（站立）构成。

items.example: Restless describes a need to move.
items.exampleCN: restless 描述想要走动的状态。

definition_zh: 甚至；连；更加；平的；偶数的；均匀的
definition_en: used to stress something surprising; also level, equal, or divisible by two
core_image: 水平的天平：两边一样高，甚至把另一边压得更低
scene: 天平左盘放着一摞书，右盘再加一枚硬币就平了。 Add one more coin and the scale will be even.
sceneCN: 这里 even 是「平的、相等的」（第 3 个义项：两边持平）；句意是再加一枚硬币天平就平了。

derivatives.zh: 由 even 加 -ly 构成，义为「均匀地；平坦地」
由 even 加 -ness 构成，义为「平坦；均匀；平静」
拼写相近但词源不同，义为「晚上」，需注意区分

senses.title: Used to stress something surprising
senses.definition: used before a surprising word or fact to emphasize it
senses.definitionCN: 放在令人意外的词或事实前加强语气
senses.example: Even the teacher could not answer the question.
senses.exampleCN: 连老师都答不出这个问题。
senses.why: The word comes from a root meaning level, and stressing works by pushing the expectation even lower or further.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「平」，强调的手法是把预期再压低、推得更远。

senses.title: Still more, comparative force
senses.definition: used before a comparative to add extra force
senses.definitionCN: 放在比较级前加强比较
senses.example: The second film was even better than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 第二部电影比第一部还要好看。
senses.why: If two things already sit on a slope, even tips the balance further toward one side.
senses.whyCN: 两物已在斜坡上，even 再把天平向一边压。

senses.title: Level, smooth or equal
senses.definition: flat, regular, or equal in amount, height or quality
senses.definitionCN: 平坦、规则，或在量、高度、质上相等
senses.example: Make sure the floor is even before laying the tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 铺瓷砖前要确保地面平整。
senses.why: This is the original meaning: two edges that sit at the same height.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：两条边处于同一高度。

senses.title: Divisible by two
senses.definition: of a number, able to be divided exactly by two
senses.definitionCN: 一个数能被二整除
senses.example: Two, four and six are even numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 二、四、六是偶数。
senses.why: Numbers paired off equally, like two matched sides of a balance, are called even.
senses.whyCN: 数能两两配对，如天平相等的两边，故称 even。

intro.en: Even is an Old English word meaning level or equal. The surprising-force use grew out of the image of pushing a balance further down.
intro.cn: even 是古英语词，本义「平、相等」。表示「甚至」的用法由「把天平再压下」的画面生长出来。

items.en: Old English efn meant 'level, equal, flat', the physical sense of matching heights.
items.cn: 古英语 efn 意为「平的、相等的、平坦的」，指高度相等的物理状态。

items.en: Middle English even kept the level sense and named numbers that pair off equally.
items.cn: 中古英语 even 保留「平」义，并用来称呼两两相配的偶数。

items.en: The adverb even appeared in the sense 'exactly, just', as in even now.
items.cn: 副词 even 出现「正是、恰恰」义，如 even now。

items.en: The stressing use, even the teacher, grew from pushing a comparison further than expected.
items.cn: 强调用法 even the teacher 源自把比较推得超出预期。

items.en: Even out and get even with extended the balance image into smoothing and repayment.
items.cn: even out 与 get even with 把天平意象延伸为抹平与扯平。

note.en: The first group collects look-alikes that only share spelling; the second collects near meanings about equality and stress.
note.cn: 第一组收集仅拼写相近的词；第二组收集与「相等、强调」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: the time before night; only shares the first letters, different root entirely
entries.definitionCN: 晚上；傍晚。仅开头拼写相同，词源完全不同。

entries.definition: something that happens; shares even- spelling from a Latin root, not related in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 事件。前缀拼写来自拉丁语，与「平」义无关。

entries.definition: the number 7; ends with the same letters by accident
entries.definitionCN: 七。词尾字母偶合，词源无关。

entries.definition: used like even to add surprise: still more, still worse
entries.definitionCN: 仍然；更加。与 even 同样可加强比较级。

entries.definition: level and smooth, close to the original physical sense
entries.definitionCN: 平的；扁平的。接近本义的物理「平」。

entries.definition: the same in size or amount, overlapping with even in equality uses
entries.definitionCN: 相等的。与 even 在「相等」义上重叠。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real level root and classroom sentences.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于「平」词根与课堂例句的具体联想。

normal.en: Learn even if first: it opens almost every concessive sentence.
normal.cn: even if＝即使，写作让步句最常用，先记短语。

normal.en: Even numbers pair off by two: two, four, six are level pairs.
normal.cn: even number 偶数：二、四、六，两两配对才「平」。

normal.en: Even better before a comparative adds real force.
normal.cn: even better 甚至更好：比较级前加 even 更有力。

normal.en: Even out returns the word to its original level meaning.
normal.cn: even out 把不平的东西抹平，回到本义。

normal.en: The sound hints at splitting even one coin equally, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一文钱也要平分」——连一文也要均分，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture two pans hanging at exactly the same height.
abstract.cn: 画面：天平两盘悬在同一高度。

abstract.en: Push one pan down further than anyone expected; that is even.
abstract.cn: 动作：把一盘压到超出所有人预期的低。

abstract.en: Feel a freshly ironed sheet, smooth without a single fold.
abstract.cn: 感觉：刚熨平的床单，平整无褶。

examples.en: Even a child can open this bottle.
examples.cn: 连小孩都能打开这个瓶子。

examples.en: Today is even colder than yesterday.
examples.cn: 今天比昨天还要冷。

examples.en: Eight is an even number.
examples.cn: 八是偶数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一「文」」——一文钱也要平分，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: even 源自古英语 efn「平的、相等的」，是纯粹的日耳曼语词，与 evening「晚上」、event「事件」词源无关，拼写相近纯属巧合。

sensesIntro.en: Even runs from physical evenness, to even numbers, to the stress words even if and even better.
sensesIntro.cn: even 从物理的「平」，到偶数，再到 even if 与 even better 的强调用法，义项由实转虚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with both pans at the same height.
core.cn: 核心意象：两盘等高的天平。

branches.en: LEVEL
branches.cn: 平整的地面与均匀的表面。

branches.en: EQUAL PAIRS
branches.cn: 能被二整除配对的偶数。

branches.en: SURPRISING DEGREE
branches.cn: 连老师都答不出的强调用法。

branches.en: PUSHED FURTHER
branches.cn: even better，比之前还要好。

branches.en: SMOOTHED OUT
branches.cn: 把差异抹平直至均匀。

intro.en: Even is a single Germanic word; its useful parts are phrases like even out rather than prefixes.
intro.cn: even 是单个日耳曼语词，其构词体现于 even out 等短语而非前后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root applies; the family is Germanic, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词与拉丁词根无关，词族属于日耳曼语，因此拉丁同源词列表为空。

items.example: Old English efn is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 efn 是直接祖先。

items.example: The evenness of the road matters for cycling.
items.exampleCN: 路面的平整对骑车很重要。

items.example: Prices even out after the rush.
items.exampleCN: 抢购过后价格趋于平稳。

items.example: He wanted to get even with the bully.
It was raining; even so, we went out.
items.exampleCN: 下着雨，即便如此我们还是出门了。

items.example: Even if it rains, the match continues.
items.exampleCN: 即使下雨，比赛照常进行。

items.meaning: a happening, from Latin e- plus venire
items.example: Event shares spelling but not the root.
items.exampleCN: event 仅拼写相近，词根不同。

definition_zh: 西；西方；西边；西部地区
definition_en: the direction where the sun goes down, and the part of a place or of the world that lies in that direction
core_image: 太阳沉到地平线后面，天边烧成一条橘红色的带子
scene: 傍晚站在田埂上，太阳正往山脊后面掉，整片天从橘红慢慢变紫。 The sun sets in the west, so the kitchen windows glow every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 west 是「西」（第 1 个义项：太阳落下的方向）；句意为太阳从西边落下，所以每天傍晚厨房的窗子都会发亮。夕阳沉到地平线后的那条橘红色带子就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 到西部去（尤指美国西部）

derivatives.zh: 西方的；西部的
向西地
最西端的

senses.title: The direction of the setting sun
senses.definition: the direction on the compass where the sun appears to go down, opposite to the east
senses.definitionCN: 指南针上太阳似乎落下的方向，与东相对
senses.example: The sun sets in the west, so the kitchen windows glow every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳从西边落下，所以每天傍晚厨房的窗户都会发亮。
senses.why: All the Germanic languages tie this word to the evening side of the sky, so the direction itself is the base sense.
senses.whyCN: 所有日耳曼语言都把这个词与天空的黄昏一侧相绑，所以「方向」本身就是最基本的意思。

senses.title: The western part of a place
senses.definition: the area of a country, town or region that lies towards the west
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家、城镇或地区中靠西的那一部分
senses.example: Heavy rain is expected in the west of the province tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚这个省的西部预计有大雨。
senses.why: Once a direction is fixed, the land lying in it takes the same name without any added ending.
senses.whyCN: 方向一旦固定，位于该方向上的土地就直接沿用同一个名字，不加任何词尾。

senses.title: The western countries
senses.definition: a loose name for Europe and North America, especially in historical and political writing
senses.definitionCN: 对欧洲与北美的笼统称呼，多用于历史与政治叙述
senses.example: Coffee reached the West through merchants in the seventeenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在十七世纪经商人之手传到西方。
senses.why: The word stopped pointing at compasses and started naming a cultural block, drawn from maps with Europe on the left.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不再指罗盘，而是指一个文化板块，这源于欧洲被画在地图左方。

senses.title: Towards the west
senses.definition: in the adverb use, moving or facing in the western direction
senses.definitionCN: 副词用法，表示朝西移动或朝向西方
senses.example: They drove west until the road ran out at the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一路向西开，直到路在海边断掉。
senses.why: English often uses a bare direction word as an adverb, so west does the work that westward does more formally.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把方向词直接当副词用，所以 west 承担了 westward 更正式地承担的工作。

intro.en: West descends from Old English west, from a Germanic base that named the evening side of the sky.
intro.cn: west 源自古英语 west，其日耳曼语词根指的是天空的黄昏一侧。

items.en: The common Germanic root carried the idea of evening and downward, so the direction was the place of the fading light.
items.cn: 共同的日耳曼词根带有「傍晚、向下」之意，因此这个方向就是光线消退之处。

items.en: Old English west was used both for the compass point and for the lands lying that way.
items.cn: 古英语 west 既指罗盘方位，也指位于该方向的土地。

items.en: The related adjective westan and the adverb westan gave English its fixed phrases for the setting sun.
items.cn: 相关的形容词与副词形式为英语留下了关于日落方向的固定说法。

items.en: The form settled as west, and compounds such as westwind and westland appeared in writing.
items.cn: 词形固定为 west，westwind、westland 等复合词也出现在文字中。

items.en: Empire and trade turned the compass point into a name for whole regions and cultures.
items.cn: 帝国与贸易把这个方位词变成了对整个地区与文化的称呼。

note.en: The first group gathers the other compass points, the second the words about western lands and movement that way.
note.cn: 第一组收其他方位词，第二组收表示西部土地与向西移动的说法。

entries.definition: The direction of sunrise, the opposite of west.
The direction to the left when one faces sunrise.
The direction to the right when one faces sunrise.
Towards the west, as a direction of travel.
The daily moment when the sun goes below the horizon.
A formal old name for the west, from the Latin word for falling.
A person who comes from the West, used in cultural talk.

normalIntro.en: The word is tied to the evening sky, so every picture of it should contain low light and a long shadow pointing the other way.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词与傍晚的天空相连，所以凡是想起它，都该带上一片低斜的光和一条指反方向的影子。

normal.en: West begins with the same sound as wet dusk air after rain.
normal.cn: west 的开头音与雨后傍晚潮湿空气的触感一样，都是 w 起头。

normal.en: The sun never says west; it just disappears there.
normal.cn: 太阳从不说「西」，它只是在那边消失。

normal.en: Maps put west on the left, the side where the page ends.
normal.cn: 地图把西放在左边，也就是纸页结束的那一侧。

normal.en: West Africa, West Lake, the West End: the same word is used as a label.
normal.cn: 西非、西湖、伦敦西区：同一个词被当作标签使用。

normal.en: Going west is going towards the light going down.
normal.cn: 向西走，就是朝着光落下的方向走。

abstract.en: Feel the last warmth on one cheek.
abstract.cn: 感觉最后一缕暖意贴在一边脸上。

abstract.en: See a shadow stretched longer than the person who casts it.
abstract.cn: 看见影子被拉得比投下它的人还长。

abstract.en: Hear the day quietly switching off.
abstract.cn: 听白昼悄悄关上开关。

examples.en: The wind blew from the west all night.
examples.cn: 风整夜都从西边吹来。

examples.en: Their farm lies to the west of the river.
examples.cn: 他们的农场位于河的西边。

examples.en: After the meeting he walked west along the main street.
examples.cn: 会议结束后，他沿着大街向西走去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂斯特」——喂，斯特先生，太阳在那边落下去了，你往那边走就是西。

root: 日耳曼语词根（黄昏、向下）→ 古英语 west（西方）→ 中古英语 west → 现代英语 west；同族有 western、westward。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the compass point of sunset, then covers the land in that direction, the cultural block called the West, and finally the bare adverb of going that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从日落方位的罗盘点出发，进而指该方向上的土地、被称为「西方」的文化板块，最后还承担了朝那边走的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an orange band of light sinking behind a ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：山脊后面一条下沉的橘色光带。

branches.en: The compass branch: the sun sets in the west.
branches.cn: 方位分支：太阳从西边落下。

branches.en: The regional branch: rain in the west of the province.
branches.cn: 地区分支：省的西部有雨。

branches.en: The cultural branch: coffee reached the West.
branches.cn: 文化分支：咖啡传到西方。

branches.en: The movement branch: driving west to the sea.
branches.cn: 移动分支：一路向西开到海边。

branches.en: The naming branch: West Africa and the west wind, all built on the point itself.
branches.cn: 命名分支：西非与西风，都直接建立在方位点之上。

intro.en: West is a free Germanic root, and its family is built with the endings -ern, -ward and -most rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: west 是自由使用的日耳曼语词根，其词族靠 -ern、-ward、-most 等词尾扩展，而不用前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for west was occidens, the falling, a participle of occidere, to go down, which is also the source of occident.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「西」的词是 occidens（落下），源自 occidere（下去）的分词，也是 occident 的来源。

items.example: It works as noun, adjective and adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作名词、形容词与副词。

items.example: It is one of the oldest compounds.
items.exampleCN: 它是最古老的复合词之一。

items.example: A capital letter marks the cultural sense.
items.exampleCN: 大写字母标示出文化义。

items.example: The plural of the directional adverb.
items.exampleCN: 方向副词加 s 的变体。

definition_zh: 块；街区；大楼；堵塞；阻挡
definition_en: a solid piece of material, a group of buildings or a town square, or to stop something moving or happening
core_image: 一块方形水泥块把门口的路挡得死死的
scene: 工地门口，一块巨大的混凝土块挡住了整条小路。 A huge block of concrete stood across the path.
sceneCN: 这里 block 是「块」（第 1 个义项：大块的固体材料）；句意为一块巨大的混凝土块横在路中间。

derivatives.zh: 由 block 加 -age 构成，义为「堵塞；阻塞物」
由 block 加 -er 构成，义为「阻挡者；封堵物」
由 block 加 -y 构成，义为「块状的；粗笨的」
由 block 与 buster 组合而成，义为「轰动一时的作品；大片」

senses.title: A solid piece
senses.definition: a large solid piece of wood, stone, concrete or similar material
senses.definitionCN: 木、石、混凝土等材料的大块固体
senses.example: He cut the meat into small blocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他把肉切成小块。
senses.why: The word first named a lump of wood or stone, and that solid piece is still the plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一块木头或石头，这个实心块状物仍是最朴素的义项。

senses.title: A town square
senses.definition: the area and buildings between two streets in a town, or the distance along it
senses.definitionCN: 城镇中两条街道之间的区域和建筑，也指这一段距离
senses.example: The bank is two blocks away.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在两个街区之外。
senses.why: American towns were laid out in square blocks, so one square of streets became a block.
senses.whyCN: 美国城镇按方形地块规划，于是一个方形街区就被称作 a block。

senses.title: A large building
senses.definition: a large building, especially one divided into flats or offices
senses.definitionCN: 大型建筑，尤指分成住宅单元或办公单元的楼
senses.example: They live in a block of flats.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一栋公寓楼里。
senses.why: A big building looks like a solid block from the street, so British English calls it a block.
senses.whyCN: 大楼从街上看就像一整块实体，所以英式英语把它叫作 block。

senses.title: To clog a passage
senses.definition: to stop a pipe, drain or passage so that nothing can pass through
senses.definitionCN: 堵住管道、排水口或通道，使任何东西都无法通过
senses.example: Leaves blocked the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 树叶堵住了排水口。
senses.why: A block of material in a pipe stops the flow, so the noun turned into a verb of clogging.
senses.whyCN: 管道里的一块东西会阻断流动，于是这个名词变成了表示堵塞的动词。

senses.title: To stop from moving
senses.definition: to stop a person, vehicle, road or plan from moving forward or happening
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人、车辆、道路或计划前进或发生
senses.example: The police blocked the road.
senses.exampleCN: 警察封锁了道路。
senses.why: From blocking a physical path, the verb widened to blocking anything that should not get through.
senses.whyCN: 从挡住实体的路，这个动词扩展到阻挡任何不该通过的事物。

intro.en: Block came into English through French from Dutch, and it has moved from wood to streets to the act of stopping.
intro.cn: block 经法语从荷兰语进入英语，并从木头一路走到街区与「阻挡」的动作。

items.en: Middle English blok came from Old French bloc, meaning a lump or a wooden block.
items.cn: 中古英语 blok 来自古法语 bloc，意思是「块」或「木块」。

items.en: Old French took it from Middle Dutch blok, the word for a tree trunk cut short.
items.cn: 古法语又取自中古荷兰语 blok，指截短的树干。

items.en: Because blocks were used in building, the word spread to stone, concrete and brick pieces.
items.cn: 由于块材用于建筑，这个词扩展到石块、混凝土块和砖块。

items.en: American towns were laid out in squares, so a square of streets became a block.
items.cn: 美国城镇按方形地块规划，于是一个方形街区成了 a block。

items.en: From stopping a passage with a block, the verb grew the sense of blocking a road, a plan or a vote.
items.cn: 从用块状物堵住通道，动词长出了封锁道路、阻挡计划或否决投票的意思。

items.en: Today block covers a solid piece, a city square, one large building and the act of stopping.
items.cn: 今天 block 覆盖实心块、城市街区、大型建筑与阻挡动作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words for pieces and obstacles.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收表示块状物与障碍的词。

entries.definition: Of the darkest colour, or without light.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「黑色的；黑暗的」，拼写与 block 相近。

entries.definition: To say that someone is responsible for something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「责怪」，拼写与 block 相近。

entries.definition: Cold, empty and without hope.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒凉的；无望的」，拼写与 block 相近。

entries.definition: A hard rectangular block used for building walls.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「砖」，指砌墙用的硬质长方形块。

entries.definition: A thick, solid piece of something.
Something that stands in the way and stops progress.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「障碍」，指挡住前进的东西。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Middle English blok came through French from Dutch blok, a tree trunk cut short.
normal.cn: 中古英语 blok 经法语来自荷兰语 blok，指截短的树干。

normal.en: Blocks were used in building, so the word spread from wood to stone and concrete.
normal.cn: 块材用于建筑，所以这个词从木头扩展到石头与混凝土。

normal.en: American towns were laid out in squares, which is why a street square is a block.
normal.cn: 美国城镇按方形规划，这就是街道方块被称作 block 的原因。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with way, office, building and out.
normal.cn: 它常与 way、office、building、out 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-l-o-c-k; the ending ck keeps the vowel short.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-l-o-c-k，结尾的 ck 让元音保持短促。

abstract.en: See a square concrete block lying across a doorway: that is block.
abstract.cn: 想象一块方形混凝土块横在门口：那就是 block。

abstract.en: Walk around that block and you have gone one city block.
abstract.cn: 绕着那块地方走一圈，你就走过了一个街区。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the square stone bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那块方石把意思带回来。

examples.en: He cut the meat into small blocks.
examples.cn: 他把肉切成小块。

examples.en: The bank is two blocks away.
examples.cn: 银行在两个街区之外。

examples.en: The police blocked the road.
examples.cn: 警察封锁了道路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「布洛克」——一块积木把门挡住：块、阻挡

root: block 经法语来自中古荷兰语 blok，原指截短的树干，后来扩展为木块、石块、混凝土块等实心块状物。因为块材用于建筑，它又指整栋大楼；美国城镇按方形地块规划，于是两条街之间的方形区域也叫 a block。由「用块状物堵住通道」，动词长出堵塞、阻挡与阻止的意思。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of block rest on one picture: a solid square that fills a space and stops what would otherwise pass.
sensesIntro.cn: block 的五个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个实心方块占住空间，挡住原本能通过的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square concrete block lying across a doorway
core.cn: 核心意象：一块方形混凝土块横在门口

branches.en: THE PIECE: the solid lump of wood or stone is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 块材线：木块或石块的实心体是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE SQUARE: a planned square of streets became a town block.
branches.cn: 街区线：规划出的方形街道区域成了城市街区。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: a large building looks like one solid block.
branches.cn: 建筑线：大型建筑看上去就是一整块实体。

branches.en: THE CLOG: material in a pipe stops the flow and gives the verb its first sense.
branches.cn: 堵塞线：管道里的材料阻断流动，给出动词第一个义项。

branches.en: THE STOP: from a blocked path the verb widened to blocking anything.
branches.cn: 阻止线：从被挡住的路，这个动词扩展到阻挡任何事物。

intro.en: Block is a base noun and verb, so the items below are its suffixes and the words it joins in compounds and phrases.
intro.cn: block 是基础名词兼动词，下面列出的是它的后缀以及构成复合词和短语时与它组合的词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word is the direct source of block; Latin moles and obstruere are recorded parallels.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词是 block 的直接来源；拉丁语 moles 与 obstruere 是有记录的平行词。

items.example: Blok is the recorded Middle English form.
items.exampleCN: blok 是有记录的中古英语形式。

definition_zh: 金；黄金；金币；金色；金牌
definition_en: a precious yellow metal, or the colour, medal or coins associated with it
core_image: 沉甸甸的黄色金属：从不生锈、人人想要
scene: 博物馆的展柜里，一枚古代金币在灯光下发亮。 The ring was made of pure gold from a famous workshop.
sceneCN: 这里 gold 是「黄金；金子」（第 1 个义项：贵重金属）；句意为这枚戒指由名坊的纯金制成。

derivatives.zh: gold 加 -en 构成，义为「金色的；金黄的」
gold 与 fish 的复合词，义为「金鱼」
gold 与 smith 的复合词，义为「金匠」

senses.title: The precious yellow metal
senses.definition: a soft precious yellow metal used for coins, jewellery and decoration
senses.definitionCN: 用于铸币、首饰与装饰的柔软贵重黄色金属
senses.example: The ring was made of pure gold from a famous workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚戒指由名坊的纯金制成。
senses.why: The core image is the heavy yellow metal that never rusts, the plain material sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是永不生锈的沉重黄色金属，是最基本的材料义项。

senses.title: Gold coins or money
senses.definition: coins made of gold, or wealth in general
senses.definitionCN: 金币或泛指财富
senses.example: Pirates buried their gold on the island.
senses.exampleCN: 海盗把金币埋在岛上。
senses.why: The metal was money itself for centuries, so coins and riches keep the name.
senses.whyCN: 数百年间这种金属就是货币本身，金币与财富便沿用其名。

senses.title: The colour of gold
senses.definition: a bright yellow colour like that of the metal
senses.definitionCN: 像黄金般的明亮黄色
senses.example: The sunset turned the whole sky gold.
senses.exampleCN: 落日把整个天空染成金色。
senses.why: The metal's colour is its most visible mark, so the colour borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 金属的颜色是最醒目的标志，颜色便借用其名。

senses.title: A gold medal or first prize
senses.definition: a medal made of or gilded with gold, given to the winner
senses.definitionCN: 给优胜者的金牌或头奖
senses.example: She won gold in the swimming final.
senses.exampleCN: 她在游泳决赛中夺得金牌。
senses.why: First place is the highest prize, and gold was always the highest metal.
senses.whyCN: 冠军是最高的奖赏，而金历来是最高等的金属。

senses.title: Made of or like gold
senses.definition: made of gold, or resembling gold in value or colour
senses.definitionCN: 由金制成，或在价值或颜色上像金
senses.example: He gave her a gold bracelet on her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 他生日那天送了她一条金手链。
senses.why: The noun turns into an adjective when the material or colour describes a thing.
senses.whyCN: 当材料或颜色修饰事物时，名词便转为形容词。

intro.en: Gold is a pure Germanic word whose deep root is debated.
intro.cn: gold 是纯正的日耳曼词，其更深的词根尚有争议。

items.en: The deepest root is uncertain; scholars debate whether it meant shining or yellow metal.
items.cn: 更深的词根不确定，学者争论其本义是「闪耀」还是「黄色金属」。

items.en: Old English gold meant the metal, already wide in use.
items.cn: 古英语 gold 指这种金属，当时已广泛使用。

items.en: Norse gull is a close relative from the same metal family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 gull 是同金属词族的近亲。

items.en: Middle English spelled it gold and added the colour and prize uses.
items.cn: 中古英语定为 gold，增加了颜色与奖赏用法。

items.en: Modern English standardized gold for metal, coins, colour, medal and adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语把 gold 统一用于金属、金币、颜色、奖牌与形容词。

note.en: The words below sound like gold or share its precious-metal field.
note.cn: 以下词与 gold 音近，或同属贵金属义场。

entries.definition: Golden in colour or value.

entries.definition: Of low temperature; one letter differs.

entries.definition: To push someone into action; sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驱使；刺激」，读音与 gold 接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A precious grey-white metal, second to gold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「银」，次于金的贵金属。

entries.definition: Valuable things stored or collected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财宝」，泛指贵重收藏。

entries.definition: Gold or silver in bulk form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「金条；银块」，未铸币的贵金属。

normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.cn: 诺斯语 gull 与德语 Gold 是英语 gold 的近亲。

normal.en: A gold medal is the top prize at the Olympic Games.

sensesIntro.cn: gold 从金属本身延伸到金币、颜色、奖牌与形容词用法。

definition_zh: 食谱；烹饪法；配方；秘诀；方法
definition_en: a set of instructions for preparing a dish, or a method for achieving something
core_image: 一张写满步骤的卡片：照着做就能端出一盘好菜
scene: 厨房里，奶奶从铁盒里抽出一张泛黄的卡片递给孙女。 Grandma handed me her secret recipe for apple pie.
sceneCN: 这里 recipe 是「食谱、配方」（第 1 个义项：做菜的步骤说明）；句意为奶奶把她做苹果派的秘方交给了我。画面里可留意：泛黄的卡片、铁盒、递过去的手。

collocations.zh: 招致灾难的做法；后患无穷

derivatives.zh: 由 re-（回来）+ cite 词根派生的同族词，义为「独奏会；朗诵」（词义已偏移到表演领域）
同根 recipere 加名词化，义为「收据；接收」（与 recipe 词义已分道）

senses.title: Instructions for cooking a dish
senses.definition: a written set of instructions telling you how to prepare and cook a particular food
senses.definitionCN: 写明如何准备和烹制某种食物的一组步骤说明
senses.example: This soup needs two eggs according to the recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 按食谱，这道汤需要放两个鸡蛋。
senses.why: The Latin root recipere means to take or receive; a recipe was originally a medical prescription, a list of things the cook or apothecary was to take.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 recipere 意为「取、拿」，recipe 最早是药方——一张列明「要取哪些材料」的单子，后来从药房转进厨房，变成照单取料做菜的步骤单。

senses.title: A formula or mixture in medicine or industry
senses.definition: a set of ingredients and proportions used to make something, especially in medicine or manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 用于制药或制造某物的成分及比例组合
senses.example: The company keeps the formula as a carefully guarded recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把这款配方当作严守的商业机密。
senses.why: Since recipes began as prescriptions written by physicians, the sense of a precise mixture of ingredients stayed in technical fields even after the cooking sense took over.
senses.whyCN: recipe 本义就是医师写下的处方， specifying 成分与比例；烹饪义普及后，这个「精确配方」义仍留在医药和工业领域，成为第二条义项。

senses.title: A method for achieving a result
senses.titleCN: 秘诀；方法（常喻好坏结果）
senses.definition: a way of doing something that will produce a particular result, often used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 能产生某种结果的做法，多用于比喻，常指带来坏结果
senses.example: Cutting sleep to five hours is a recipe for exhaustion.
senses.exampleCN: 把睡眠压缩到五个小时，只会换来疲惫不堪。
senses.why: A formula reliably produces its product; by metaphor, any reliable combination of actions 'produces' an outcome, whether good or bad.
senses.whyCN: 配方按固定比例就能稳定产出成品；比喻开来，一套固定的行事组合也会稳定「产出」某种结局，所以引申出「注定导致……的做法」。

intro.en: Recipe comes from Latin recipere, and it began life not in the kitchen but in the pharmacy.
intro.cn: recipe 源自拉丁语 recipere（取、拿），它的出生地不是厨房，而是药房。

items.en: recipere, from re- (back) + capere (to take), meant 'to take back, receive'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 recipere 由 re-（回）+ capere（拿）构成，意为「取回、接收」。

items.en: In medical manuscripts, recipes began with the imperative 'Recipe!' — 'Take (the following ingredients)'.
items.cn: 在中世纪医学手稿里，药方以命令式 Recipe! 开头，意为「取下列药材」。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as a term on physicians' prescriptions.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语，仍指医师处方上的用语。

items.en: English took over the word in the 14th century, first for medical prescriptions.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，最初仍指药方、处方。

items.en: By the 17th to 18th centuries the cooking sense dominated, and later the figurative sense 'a recipe for disaster' appeared.
items.cn: 十七到十八世纪起烹饪义占主流，后来又出现「招致灾难的做法」这类比喻用法。

note.en: These words are often confused with recipe because of spelling or meaning.
note.cn: 下列词与 recipe 或形近易混，或义场相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 收据；接收（与 recipe 拼写极近，词源同族但词义不同）

entries.definition: to say aloud a poem or list from memory
entries.definitionCN: 背诵；朗诵（只是拼写相近，词源为 citare「唤起」，并非同源）

entries.definition: a person who receives something
entries.definitionCN: 接受者；受领者（同出 recipere 词族）

entries.definition: a fixed form of words or a set of ingredients for a result
entries.definitionCN: 公式；配方（偏技术、固定化）

entries.definition: a doctor's written order for medicine
entries.definitionCN: 处方（recipe 的现代医学对应词）

entries.definition: a planned way of doing something
entries.definitionCN: 方法；办法（泛指做法，不限材料配比）

normalIntro.en: Root-based reminders for recipe.
normalIntro.cn: recipe 的词根式记忆提示。

normal.en: re- (back) + cip (take) + e: what you 'take' to make the dish.
normal.cn: re-（回）+ cip（拿）+ e：照单「取」来下锅的，就是食谱。

normal.en: Same root family as receive, receipt, recipient.
normal.cn: 与 receive、receipt、recipient 同属「拿取」词族。

normal.en: Medieval prescriptions began with 'Recipe!' meaning 'take these'.
normal.cn: 中世纪药方开头就是 Recipe!（取药），可见词的本义。

normal.en: Collocation anchor: a recipe for disaster = a formula producing disaster.
normal.cn: 搭配锚点：a recipe for disaster，即「产出灾难的配方」。

normal.en: Compare receipt: both from recipere, but one proves payment.
normal.cn: 对照 receipt：同根不同义，receipt 是付款凭证。

abstract.en: Picture a yellowed card in grandma's tin box, steps written in ink.
abstract.cn: 想象奶奶铁盒里那张泛黄的卡片，墨水写着一步步的做法。

abstract.en: Imagine a pharmacist shouting 'Take!' at shelves of herbs.
abstract.cn: 想象药剂师对着药草架喊一声「取！」，那是 recipe 的起点。

abstract.en: See ingredients pouring into one pot in fixed ratios.
abstract.cn: 看见材料按固定比例倒进同一口锅——配方即比例。

examples.en: Follow the recipe step by step and the bread will rise.
examples.cn: 照着食谱一步步做，面包就能发起来。

examples.en: Her secret recipe has been passed down for four generations.
examples.cn: 她的秘方已经传了四代人。

examples.en: Ignoring the weather forecast is a recipe for disaster on a mountain trip.
examples.cn: 登山不看天气预报，注定要出乱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞塞皮」——「瑞士塞来的皮」配方要照单取料；联想成一张塞到手里的配方卡，记 recipe 是「食谱、配方」。

root: 拉丁语 recipere（取、拿）：re-（回）+ capere（拿）。recipe 原为处方用语 Recipe!（取下列药材），后转为食谱与配方义；同根词 receive、receipt、recipient。

sensesIntro.en: From pharmacy to kitchen to figurative speech: recipe keeps its core image of 'take exactly what is listed'.
sensesIntro.cn: 从药房到厨房再到比喻：recipe 的核心意象始终是「照单取料」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: take exactly what the list says
core.cn: 核心意象：照单取料，按固定清单行事

branches.en: Cooking instructions built from a list of ingredients.
branches.cn: 以材料清单为基础的烹饪步骤（义项 01）。

branches.en: A precise mixture in medicine or industry.
branches.cn: 医药或工业领域的精确配方（义项 02）。

branches.en: A formula reliably yields its product.
branches.cn: 配方按固定比例稳定产出（义项 02、03）。

branches.en: Figurative: a way of doing things predicts the outcome.
branches.cn: 比喻义：固定做法预示结局（义项 03）。

branches.en: Recipes and disaster formulas both promise a result.
branches.cn: 食谱与「灾难配方」都承诺一个结果（义项 01、03）。

intro.en: Recipe carries the Latin take-structure re- + cap.
intro.cn: recipe 携带拉丁语「取拿」结构 re- + cap。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives from capere (to take).
latinIntro.cn: 来自 capere（拿取）的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a list of what to take

definition_zh: 邮件；信件；邮政系统；电子邮件；锁子甲；邮寄
definition_en: letters and parcels sent by post; the postal system; electronic messages; armour of linked metal rings; to send something by post

scene: 雨下了一整夜，门廊的脚垫上积着水，伞桶旁边多了一只湿透的牛皮纸袋。 The mail had been pushed through the slot and now lay in a damp heap on the floor.
sceneCN: 这里指寄来的信件与包裹（第 1 个义项：邮件）；句意为邮件从投信口塞进来，湿漉漉地堆在地板上。

pos.zh: 邮件；信件；邮政系统；电子邮件；锁子甲

derivatives.zh: 由 mail 加 -er 构成，义为「邮寄者；邮递包装」
由 mail 加 -ing 构成，义为「邮寄；寄出的邮件」
由 electronic 的首字母 e 与 mail 复合，义为「电子邮件；发电子邮件」
由 mail 与 box 复合，义为「邮箱；信箱」

senses.title: Letters and parcels sent by post
senses.definition: letters, cards and parcels delivered through the postal system
senses.definitionCN: 通过邮政系统投递的信件、卡片和包裹
senses.example: The mail arrives before noon on weekdays.
senses.exampleCN: 工作日里邮件在中午前送到。
senses.why: The word first named the travelling bag that carried letters, and the contents of the bag took the name of the bag.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指装信件的旅行袋，后来袋中之物沿用了袋子的名字。

senses.title: The postal system
senses.definition: the public service that collects and delivers letters and parcels
senses.definitionCN: 负责收寄和投递信件、包裹的公共服务
senses.example: The island has no daily mail service in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛在冬天没有每日邮政服务。
senses.why: Once the bag and its contents were called mail, the network that moved them took the same name, because the service existed to handle the mail.
senses.whyCN: 袋子及其内容物都叫 mail 之后，负责运送它们的网络也用了同一个名字，因为这项服务的存在就是为了处理邮件。

senses.title: Electronic messages
senses.definition: messages sent and received through the internet, especially in an email account
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网收发、存放在电子邮件账户里的信息
senses.example: Her mail was full of unread messages after the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 假期过后，她的邮箱里全是未读信息。
senses.why: Electronic messages borrowed the name because they arrive in an inbox, just as paper letters arrive through a letterbox.
senses.whyCN: 电子消息借用这个名字，因为它们进入收件箱，就像纸质信件从信箱口进来一样。

senses.title: Armour of interlinked metal rings
senses.definition: flexible armour made of small metal rings linked into a mesh
senses.definitionCN: 由小金属环连接成网、可以随身体弯曲的铠甲
senses.example: The knight's mail protected him from a glancing sword blow.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士的锁子甲挡下了一记擦过的剑击。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word: Old French maille meant a mesh, from Latin macula, and linked rings form exactly such a mesh.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词：古法语 maille 意为网眼，源自拉丁语 macula，而环环相扣的金属正构成这样的网。

senses.title: To send something by post
senses.definition: to put a letter or parcel into the postal system for delivery
senses.definitionCN: 把信件或包裹交给邮政系统投递
senses.example: Please mail the signed form before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五之前把签好的表格寄出去。
senses.why: The verb is simply the noun put to work: to mail something is to hand it over to the mail.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词直接转用：mail 某物，就是把它交给邮政系统。

intro.en: Mail is two words under one spelling: a bag word that became letters and postal service, and a mesh word that became armour.
intro.cn: mail 是同一拼写下的两个词：一个「袋子」词变成信件与邮政，一个「网眼」词变成铠甲。

items.en: The postal sense starts from Old French male, a bag or wallet carried on a journey.
items.cn: 邮政义从古法语 male 开始，那是旅途中携带的袋子或钱袋。

items.en: The bag word is usually traced to a reconstructed Frankish form such as *malha, though the exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个「袋子」词一般追溯到重构的法兰克语形式（如 *malha），但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: The armour sense comes from a different Old French word, maille, meaning a mesh or ring.
items.cn: 铠甲义来自另一个古法语词 maille，意为网眼或环。

items.en: Latin macula meant a spot or a mesh in a net, and it is the recorded source of maille.
items.cn: 拉丁语 macula 意为斑点或网中的网眼，是 maille 有记载的来源。

items.en: Modern English keeps both histories under one spelling and adds email, a new sense built on the postal one.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条历史并排在同一种拼写下，并新增了建立在邮政义上的 email。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives of the postal word; the near-meaning group gathers words for letters and for sending them.
note.cn: 形近组收邮政义词的复合词与派生词；近义组收表示信件与寄送的词。

entries.definition: Electronic mail; also the verb for sending it.
entries.definitionCN: 电子邮件；也指发送电子邮件的动作。

entries.definition: A box or address where mail is received.
entries.definitionCN: 接收邮件的箱子或地址。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to deliver mail.
entries.definitionCN: 以投递邮件为职业的人。

entries.definition: A bag used to carry letters and parcels.
entries.definitionCN: 用来装信件和包裹的袋子。

entries.definition: The public system for sending letters, or to send a letter.
entries.definitionCN: 寄信的公共系统，或指寄信。

entries.definition: A written message sent to someone, usually on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 写给某人的书面信息，通常写在纸上。

entries.definition: An object or set of objects wrapped for sending.
entries.definitionCN: 包装好准备寄送的物品。

entries.definition: Letters exchanged between people.

normalIntro.en: The word carries a bag, a bundle of letters, a postal network, an inbox and a coat of rings, all under one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时装着袋子、信件、邮政网络、收件箱和一件环甲，全部共用一种拼写。

normal.en: Mail first meant a travelling bag, so the word began with a container rather than with paper.
normal.cn: mail 最初指旅行袋，所以这个词的起点是容器，而不是纸张。

normal.en: The postal sense and the armour sense look identical but have separate histories, one from a bag and one from a mesh.
normal.cn: 邮政义和铠甲义拼写相同，却各有来历：一个出自袋子，一个出自网眼。

normal.en: Old French maille and Latin macula connect the armour to a net of rings, which is why chain mail is described as a mesh.
normal.cn: 古法语 maille 与拉丁语 macula 把铠甲连到环网，所以锁子甲被形容为网。

normal.en: Email simply puts the prefix e- for electronic in front of mail, keeping the old idea of messages waiting for you.
normal.cn: email 只是把表示电子的前缀 e- 放在 mail 前面，保留了「消息在等你」的旧意象。

normal.en: Mail carrier and mail order show the word naming both the thing delivered and the system that delivers it.
normal.cn: mail carrier 与 mail order 表明这个词既指被投递的东西，也指投递它的系统。

abstract.en: A wet bundle of envelopes on a doormat makes the abstract postal system visible for a moment.
abstract.cn: 门垫上湿漉漉的一叠信封，让抽象的邮政系统在一瞬间变得可见。

abstract.en: A bag becomes letters, letters become a service, and the service becomes an inbox: one name travels the whole route.
abstract.cn: 袋子变成信件，信件变成服务，服务又变成收件箱：一个名字走完了整条路线。

abstract.en: Chain mail and posted mail share only a spelling; remembering that they are strangers keeps both meanings clear.
abstract.cn: 锁子甲与邮寄的邮件只共享拼写；记住它们是陌生人，两个意思才不会混。

examples.en: The mail arrives before noon on weekdays.
examples.cn: 工作日里邮件在中午前送到。

examples.en: Please mail the signed form before Friday.
examples.cn: 请在周五之前把签好的表格寄出去。

examples.en: The knight's mail protected him from a glancing sword blow.
examples.cn: 骑士的锁子甲挡下了一记擦过的剑击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妹儿」——把信交给小妹儿去寄；记住 mail 是邮件、邮寄。

root: 邮政义一般认为来自古法语 male（旅行袋）；铠甲义来自古法语 maille（网眼），后者可追溯到拉丁语 macula。两条来源在英语里拼成同一个词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is letters in transit; the postal service, the electronic inbox and the verb all grow from it, while the armour sense follows a separate Latin line.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是运送中的信件；邮政系统、电子收件箱与动词都由此长出，而铠甲义则走另一条拉丁线索。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of envelopes on a doormat and an old cloth bag that once carried them.
core.cn: 核心意象：门垫上的一叠信封，以及一只曾经装过这些信件的旧布袋。

branches.en: a damp stack of envelopes on a doormat
branches.cn: 门垫上湿漉漉的一叠信封

branches.en: a post office truck moving through a winter village
branches.cn: 邮车穿过冬日村庄

branches.en: an inbox glowing with unread messages
branches.cn: 收件箱里亮着未读消息

branches.en: a knight's sleeve of linked rings catching the light
branches.cn: 骑士衣袖上的连环映着光

branches.en: a hand dropping a signed form into a letterbox
branches.cn: 一只手把签好的表格投进信箱

intro.en: The word is held together by a bag noun from Old French, a mesh noun from Latin, and English compounds that extend both lines.
intro.cn: 这个词由古法语的「袋子」名词、拉丁语的「网眼」名词，以及延伸两条线索的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Only the armour sense has a Latin source: maille comes from macula, a word for a spot or a mesh.
latinIntro.cn: 只有铠甲义有拉丁语来源：maille 出自 macula，一个表示斑点或网眼的词。
